items.text: pg. 1 JOHNSON COUNTY Department of Planning & Zoning Phone: (317) 346-4350 86 West Court Street www.co.johnson.in.us Franklin, Indiana 46131 MEETING AGENDA Johnson County Advisory Plan Commission August 24th, 2026 - 6:00 PM Public Auditorium, West Annex Building 86 West Court Street, Franklin, Indiana CALL TO ORDER ROLL CALL APPROVAL of MINUTES Approval of minutes from the March 23, 2026 meeting. OTHER APPOINTMENTS PUBLIC HEARINGS -CONTINUED HEARINGS- -NEW HEARINGS – W-3-26 Coy Waiver, 3131 S 350 W, Trafalgar WAIVER of the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to provide for a potential two-lot Minor Subdivision with one of the lots having a depth-to-width ratio of 2.2:1 Unified Development Ordinance Amendments – The proposed changes cover key operational areas including statutory protections for shooting ranges, defined standards for event centers and group homes, clarification of accessory dwelling unit and structure sizes, and relief from suburban standards (such as sidewalks and individual lot landscaping) in rural and agricultural zoning districts. OLD BUSINESS NEW BUSINESS REPORTS and RECOMMENDATIONS pg. 2 ADJOURNMENT The next meeting of the Johnson County Advisory Plan Commission is scheduled for September 28th, 2026 at 6:00 PM in the public auditorium of the Courthouse West Annex Building. LIVE STREAMING AVAILABLE HERE Meeting ID: 853 5483 6693 Passcode: 057410 (Link can also be found on the County Website under Events Calendar – Click on Events Website) In accordance with American Disabilities Act, any person attending the public meeting in need of reasonable accommodations in order to attend, hear, or present evidence at the public meeting on an agenda item should contact the Johnson County ADA coordinator, Barb Davis, at 86 W. Court St., Franklin, IN 46131, (317) 346-4329, bdavis@co.johnson.in.us. Pursuant to Indiana Code 5-14-9 (the “Act”), board member terms and appointing authority: Johnson County Plan Commission Appointment Member Appointing Authority Term Ron West Representative County Commissioner 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Jonathan T. Myers Representative County Council 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Ron Bates Alternate Member - County Council 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Greg Cantwell Surveyor - Office Held Office Term Shalee Bradley ANR County Extension Agent - Office Held Office Term Charles Canary Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2023 - 12/31/2027 Douglas Gray Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2024 - 12/31/2027 Steven Hickman Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2023 - 12/31/2027 Robert Page Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2024 - 12/31/2027 Stoney Vann Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2025 - 12/31/2028 Staff Report CASE NUMBER: W-3-26, Coy Waiver ADDRESS: 3131 S 350 W, Trafalgar PETITIONER: Dale & Jacqueline Coy by Barkocy Surveying, Inc REQUEST WAIVER of the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to provide for a potential two-lot Minor Subdivision with one of the lots having a depth-to-width ratio of 2.2:1 (in Minor Subdivisions, lots with an area less than five acres may have a depth-to-width ratio no greater than 2:1) STAFF RECOMMENDATION Staff recommends approval of this request. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION The subject property is 7.2 acres parcel in Hensley Township. The site is zoned SR (Single-Family Residential) and is currently improved with a single-family dwelling and a few accessory structures. The parcel is bordered by larger track of land used agriculturally. WAIVER REQUEST The petitioners are requesting a waiver from the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) subdivision lot arrangement standards to create a two-lot minor subdivision.  Lot 1: Proposed at 2.00 acres, containing an existing residential dwelling.  Lot 2: Proposed at 4.92 acres, containing existing accessory structures, mature trees, and a driveway. Per the UDO, lots under 5.0 acres in size are required to maintain a maximum depth-to-width ratio of 2:1.  Intent of Standard: The depth-to-width ratio requirement is designed to prevent "bowling alley" or "flag shape" lots, ensuring that parcels maintain functional, buildable proportions rather than overly narrow configurations. It discourages irregular lot boundaries designed solely to satisfy dimensional metrics on paper, promoting straightforward, clean lot lines that simplify property maintenance, access, and land ownership disputes over time. Lot 1: Meets all UDO lot ratio and dimensional standards. Lot 2: At 4.92 acres, Lot 2 falls just 0.08 acres short of the 5-acre threshold where depth-to-width standards no longer apply. The proposed lot measures 280 feet in width by 615 feet in depth, resulting in a depth-to-width ratio of 2.2 to 1. Staff Analysis & Findings To satisfy the strict 2:1 ratio (requiring a minimum lot width of ~307.5 feet for a 615-foot depth), the applicant evaluated an alternate layout. That compliant layout would require an artificial "bump-out" into Lot 1 near the road frontage (extending width to 307 feet for approximately 40 feet) before narrowing back down. Staff finds that strict compliance via this alternate layout creates undesirable planning outcomes:  It introduces an irregular property line configuration solely to satisfy a technical metric on paper.  It causes the shared property line to intersect existing site improvements, including an established driveway and mature tree line, necessitating unnecessary cross-access or boundary easements. Granting the requested waiver to allow a 2.2:1 ratio allows for a clean, straight interior lot line that keeps existing site features intact on Lot 2 without creating awkward lot geometries along the public road frontage. The deviation from the standard is minor (2.2:1 vs 2:1) and presents no adverse impacts on surrounding properties, public safety, or traffic flow. FINDINGS OF FACT, STAFF ANALYSIS The granting of the waiver will not be detrimental to the public safety, health, or welfare or be injurious to nearby property; The granting of this waiver will not be detrimental to public safety, health, or welfare, nor will it be injurious to nearby properties. The requested depth-to-width ratio adjustment applies solely to an internal lot configuration (Lot 2) and will not negatively impact surrounding properties, public safety, or existing public infrastructure. The waiver requested will not affect the area adjacent to the property in a substantially adverse manner because: The requested waiver is a minor numeric deviation (a 2.2:1 ratio vs. the required 2:1 ratio) on a 4.92-acre lot that falls just 0.08 acres short of the 5-acre threshold where the rule no longer applies. The adjustment does not increase density, alter permitted land uses, or change the rural character of the immediate area. The conditions upon which the request for a waiver are based are unique to the property for which the waiver is sought and are not applicable generally to other properties. The subject parcel features long-established physical improvements, including an existing driveway and mature tree line serving Lot 2. Designing a fully compliant 2:1 lot would require introducing irregular "jogs" or a temporary bump-out along the road frontage, creating unnecessary cross-boundary encumbrances that are unique to this specific site layout. The strict application of the terms of the Unified Development Ordinance will result in unnecessary hardship because: Strict application of the UDO ratio would force the applicant to place the shared lot line through the existing driveway and mature trees. This would require creating unnecessary cross-access and maintenance easements between the two parcels. Alternatively, forcing a compliant 2:1 lot width near the road frontage results in an irregular, unnatural property line configuration solely to satisfy a paper metric. The waiver is not primarily for the economic benefit of the petitioner because: The request is strictly driven by sound land planning principles to achieve a logical, straight-line property boundary that keeps existing physical improvements (driveway and trees) entirely on the lot they serve. The waiver request is not due to a hardship caused by the current owner of the property. The existing driveway and mature tree lines predate the current owner's acquisition of the land. The hardship stems from adapting an established residential site to modern UDO dimensional standards rather than any recent action taken by the petitioner. The waiver will not, in any manner, contravene provisions of the Zoning Ordinance, Comprehensive Plan, or Official Map, as interpreted by the Commission. The proposed minor subdivision complies with all underlying zoning standards, including minimum lot area, lot width, and setback requirements for both proposed lots. The request represents a slight numerical variance (2.2:1 vs. 2:1) on a parcel that is only 0.08 acres short of the 5-acre threshold where depth-to-width limits cease to apply. Approval of the waiver aligns with the Comprehensive Plan by encouraging orderly growth, preserving existing site improvements, and avoiding irregular property geometries along public rights-of-way. GENERAL INFORMATION Subdivider: Dale and Jacquline Coy 3131 S 350 W Trafalgar IN 46181 Owner: Same Current Zoning: SR Single Family Residential Existing Land Use: Single-family residential Future Land Use: Rural Residential -MNH W-3-26 Base Map Subject Site W-3-26 Base Map II W-3-26 SUBJECT PROPERTY W-3-26 Petitioner’s Findings of Facts © 2026 Microsoft Corporation © Maxar ©CNES (2026) Distribution Airbus DS © 2026 TMAP MOBILITY Earthstar Geographics SIO © Mapbox 4800 West Smith Valley Road, Suite O * Greenwood, IN 46142 Office - 317-881-3898 * www.BarkocySurveying.com BARKOCY W N E S S U R V E Y I N G I N C . professional land surveying & land development services 4800 West Smith Valley Road, Suite O * Greenwood, IN 46142 Office - 317-881-3898 * www.BarkocySurveying.com BARKOCY W N E S S U R V E Y I N G I N C . professional land surveying & land development services UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE – 2026 Amendment proposal The Department of Planning and Zoning has prepared a series of proposed text amendments to the Johnson County Uniﬁed Development Ordinance (UDO). Following the comprehensive adoption of the UDO in 2024, staff have identiﬁed several areas requiring technical cleanup, administrative clariﬁcation, and legislative updates. The proposed changes cover key operational areas including statutory protections for shooting ranges, deﬁned standards for event centers and group homes, clariﬁcation of accessory dwelling unit and structure sizes, and relief from suburban standards (such as sidewalks and individual lot landscaping) in rural and agricultural zoning districts.  Draft Redline Version of UDO Amendments as of 8-14-26  List of track changes to the UDO Shooting / Archery Range – Indoor Rationale: Amendments were incorporated pursuant to Senate Enrolled Act (SEA) 176, which establishes protections for existing shooting ranges to ensure they may continue operating without being subject to non-conforming restrictions when modiﬁed. The legislation also mandates that shooting ranges and sporting goods stores be permitted by right in designated zoning districts, subject to speciﬁc conditions. Affected Sections: Pages 15, 17, 27, 29, 31, 115, 246, and Appendix A. Event Centers Rationale: Event centers (deﬁned as facilities hosted for private gatherings, parties, celebrations, and family events) were added as a distinct, described land use within the UDO. Staff routinely receives inquiries regarding this use, but the ordinance previously lacked clear operational guidance and dimensional standards. This amendment deﬁnes "Event Center" and establishes the speciﬁc zoning districts where the use is permitted. Affected Sections: Pages 15, 27, 29, 236, and Appendix A. Accessory Dwelling Units. Rationale: Proposed revisions to the Accessory Dwelling Unit standards provide clarity and prevent unintentional misinterpretation: Density Limits: Attached and detached ADUs were previously listed separately, with individual provisions stating a quantity of "one" was permitted. To prevent interpretations that a single property could construct both an attached and a detached ADU, the word "or detached/attached" was inserted to clarify that only one ADU type is permitted per lot. Addressing Standards: Revised the addressing provision to clarify that obtaining a distinct address for an ADU is optional (upon request by the property owner) rather than mandatory. Affected Sections: Page 93. Accessory Structure Rationale: Prior to the 2024 UDO adoption, the county ordinance regulated accessory structures based on the aggregate square footage of all structures on a lot. This provision was incorrectly converted during the 2024 update, leading to conﬂicting interpretations. The proposed text restores the original intent by clarifying that the combined gross ﬂoor area of all accessory structures on a parcel shall not exceed the designated size threshold. Affected Sections: Page 95. Group Home and Nursing Homes Rationale: Updates were made to the group home standards to align county zoning regulations better with ADA and federal fair housing guidelines, while resolving internal code inconsistencies across residential zoning districts. Deﬁnition & Scale: The UDO explicitly distinguishes a Group Home from larger institutional facilities, such as commercial nursing or convalescent centers. This distinction ensures group homes operate within a typical residential scale and character. State Compliance: Standards were updated to reference appropriate state licensing bodies—speciﬁcally the Division of Disability and Rehabilitative Services (DDRS) and the Division of Mental Health and Addiction (DMHA)—ensuring local oversight supports, rather than conﬂicts with, state licensing mandates. Permitted Districts & Occupancy Caps: Clariﬁed standards across residential and agricultural districts. Occupancy remains capped at eight (8) residents (excluding support staff) to maintain compatibility with single-family residential neighborhoods while ensuring compliance with federal Fair Housing Act protections for group living arrangements. Permitting & Review Process: Streamlined the review framework to clarify when a facility is permitted by right versus when it requires special approval, eliminating previous ambiguity surrounding unlisted uses or special exception requirements for state-licensed residential care homes. Affected Sections: Pages 15, 17,,19,21,23,27 105, 112,236,238,240, and Appendix A. Minimum Development Size for Commercial and Industrial Land Rationale: The 2024 UDO update introduced a minimum acreage threshold for commercial and industrial developments. Upon reviewing recent major plat ﬁlings and waiver requests, Staff identiﬁed that most existing commercial and industrial parcels in the county do not meet this minimum acreage requirement and are not adjacent to parcels that could be combined to meet it. While encouraging coordinated, large-scale development is ideal, this standard inadvertently prevents viable property divisions on smaller lots and is uncommonly restrictive compared to peer jurisdictions. Staff recommends deleting this requirement. Affected Sections: Pages 128 and 129. Deﬁnitions added Rationale: Restored deﬁnitions from the 2002 Zoning Ordinance to better deﬁne "front yard" and "lot lines" for setback calculations. Additionally, modiﬁed the general setback deﬁnition to clarify that setback regulations apply to all structures, not just primary buildings. Minor Text Amendments & Technical Fixes Page 38 (I-69 Corridor Overlay Setback): Re-established the I-69 setback requirement within the Corridor Overlay District. The prior zoning ordinance was drafted before Interstate 69 was constructed, and this overlay provision was inadvertently omitted during the 2024 UDO adoption. Pages 67–68 (Individual Lot Landscaping): Removed individual lot landscaping requirements for Agricultural (A) and Agricultural-Residential (A-R) zoned properties. These standards are intended for major/minor residential subdivisions rather than rural, agricultural acreage. Page 87 (Inoperable Vehicle Storage): Reverted inoperable vehicle storage standards for A and A-R districts back to pre-2024 regulations (allowing one inoperable vehicle per property without full screening requirements). The 2024 UDO requirement for complete visual screening will now apply primarily to suburban and commercial districts, aligning with county policy prioritizing reduced enforcement in rural areas. Page 130 (Sidewalk Requirements): Removed mandatory sidewalk installation for minor subdivisions. Because the majority of minor subdivisions occur in rural areas where sidewalk networks do not exist, this requirement routinely resulted in unnecessary waiver requests.

JOHNSON COUNTY Department of Planning and Zoning (317) 346-4350 86 West Court Street www.JohnsonCounty.in.gov Franklin, Indiana 46131 Courthouse Annex MEETING AGENDA Johnson County Board of Zoning Appeals September 29th, 2026, 6:00 PM Public Auditorium, West Annex Building 86 West Court Street, Franklin, Indiana CALL TO ORDER ROLL CALL APPROVAL of MINUTES Meeting minutes from the July 28th 2026 meeting PUBLIC HEARINGS The Board will begin with New Petitions at 6:00 PM in accordance with the published public notice. VARIANCE OF DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS from the Johnson County Uniﬁed Development Ordinance to allow a reduction of the required side yard setback from 10 feet to 5 feet for an accessory structure in the SR, Single- Family Residential zoning district. OLD BUSINESS None. NEW BUSINESS REPORTS AND RECOMMENDATIONS None. ADJOURNMENT The next regular meeting of the Johnson County Board of Zoning Appeals is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27th, 2026, at 7:00 PM. LIVE STREAMING AVAILABLE HERE Meeting ID: 870 6549 8518 Passcode: 100889 (Link can also be found on the County Website under Events Calendar – Click on Events Website) 2 Staff Report CASE NUMBER: V-07-26 ADDRESS: 5362 Warrior Trail, Whiteland, Parcel #: 41-05-23-041-023.000-033 PETITIONER: Sandhu Properties INC, By Chad Leinart ADDENDUM FOR SEPTEMBER BOARD MEETING The subject property has been cleaned up, and all improper land uses have ceased. All unauthorized materials and activities have been removed from the site, the house has been secured and boarded up, and access points have been blocked to prevent further unauthorized use. The property has remained in full compliance with the Board’s motion and applicable zoning regulations since the June Board of Zoning Appeals meeting. This petition was previously continued by the Board to allow the petitioner time to demonstrate active efforts to abate all unpermitted uses prior to formal approval. Aside from the site cleanup and securing of the property, no other changes or modifications have been submitted regarding the application. All other findings, details, and recommendations in the original Staff Report remain unchanged REQUEST VARIANCE OF USE of the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to allow for a trucking parking and trucking facility business (not permitted in a GB-zoned property). PROPERTY DESCRIPTION This variance request involves a 12.696-acre parcel zoned GB (General Business). The property is currently unimproved, though it contains an existing dwelling that is not being used for residential purposes. The land is currently being utilized for parking. Surrounding land uses include: South: Several semi-tractor oriented businesses. North: Semi Parking, Warehouse, and manufacturing uses, including a similar use approved in 2023 by the Board of Zoning Appeals. All affected parcels, with the exception of 5440 Warrior Trail, are located within the Town of Whiteland limits VARIANCE OF USE REQUEST If approved, this Variance of Use request would allow the property to be redeveloped as a commercial truck parking lot, with the potential to repurpose the existing structure for fleet operations. Proposed Site Plan & Operations Parking Capacity: The submitted site plan proposes parking for approximately 71 semi-trucks and semi-trailers. Structure Reuse: The existing structure is proposed to be converted into an office building. 3 Technical Review Adjustments: The final number of parking spots may be reduced during the Technical Review Committee (TRC) review of the civil plans to ensure compliance with development standards, including parking lot setbacks, landscaping, and drainage requirements. Hours of Operation: According to the petitioner’s submitted Plan of Operation, the facility will operate 24 hours a day with security. REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS The development will be required to go through the Technical Review Committee process and must adhere to the following:  All commercial standards in the zoning ordinance.  Procurement of a State Design Release for commercial use of the existing building.  Full compliance with all requirements of the Stormwater Management Ordinance. STAFF NOTES AND RECOMMENDATION This property has been continuously used for truck parking without authorization from staff, despite repeated enforcement notices from the department. However, staff notes that this formal application indicates the property owners are now making an effort to correct past violations and establish a compliant parking facility. If approved, this process will ensure the development is better suited for the area in both appearance and operational use. The existing dwelling on the property has previously been used by the property owner and guests as a social gathering spot, which has presented ongoing issues for the Town of Whiteland. The house is currently unfit for occupation. This unauthorized use must cease immediately, regardless of the outcome of this variance request. The Town of Whiteland has provided an official response to this use request, which is attached to this staff report for review. The requested variance is consistent with and similar to the uses of adjoining properties. Staff recommends the following conditions for consideration: 1. Required Approvals: The development must obtain all required permits and approvals before any improvements are made to the property. 2. Cease Existing Operations: All current semi-truck parking on the property must be removed until proper permits have been issued and site improvements are completed. 3. Structure Occupancy: The existing structure cannot be occupied or used until proper commercial permits have been obtained. 4. Nuisance Mitigation: If the structure is not brought into commercial use within one (1) year of this approval, it must be demolished and removed from the property to deter improper use and prevent a public nuisance. 4 5. Town Interlocal Agreement: The development must include and adhere to all stipulations provided by the Town of Whiteland. STAFF VARIANCE OF USE FINDINGS OF FACT: STAFF ANALYSIS 1. The approval will not be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community. The proposed conversion of the property into a secure, 24-hour commercial semi-truck parking facility will not be injurious to the public health, safety, or general welfare, provided all staff conditions are met. The property will undergo a rigorous Technical Review Committee (TRC) process to ensure proper drainage, stormwater management, landscaping, and setbacks are implemented. Furthermore, requiring the unapproved, hazardous use of the existing residential structure to cease and mandating its removal if not developed within one year directly mitigates an existing public nuisance and improves community safety. 2. The use and value of the area adjacent to the property included in the variance will not be affected in a substantially adverse manner. The proposed use is highly consistent with the established character of the immediate area. The property is bordered to the south and north by semi-tractor-oriented businesses. By bringing this site into compliance through formal development standards, the physical appearance and operational safety of the site will be significantly upgraded compared to its current unauthorized state, thereby protecting adjacent property values. 3. The need for the variance does arise from some condition peculiar to the property involved. The 12.696-acre parcel is currently zoned GB (General Business), which does not permit the transportation and logistics support uses that have become dominant in this immediate area. Due to the intense semi-tractor traffic and industrial warehouse operations directly bordering the site to the north and south, it is highly impractical for this property to be developed for any of the retail or light commercial uses standardly permitted in the GB district. The unique physical location of the parcel—effectively locked within a heavy industrial and transportation corridor—creates a distinct peculiarity where standard general business uses are no longer viable or compatible. 4. The strict application of the terms of the Zoning Ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which variance is sought. Strict adherence to the GB zoning text would restrict the property from fulfilling its most logical economic use as a support facility for the surrounding transport sector. Forcing standard retail or office development on a site locked between semi-truck facilities and manufacturing warehouses creates an unnecessary hardship, as such businesses would struggle with compatibility. Granting the variance allows the petitioner to formalize and legally rectify the land use in a way that matches the market reality of the corridor. 5. The approval does not interfere substantially with the Comprehensive Plan. 5 The Comprehensive Plan’s recommendation for mixed use in this area. Mixed uses development is intended to encourage a well-planned, integrated mix of compatible uses that relate well and support one another. This use is compatible with other uses in the area. GENERAL INFORMATION Applicant: Chad Leinart 3200 Sycamore Ct, Ste 2A Columbus IN 47203 Owner: Sandhu Properties Inc 5362 Warrior Trl Whiteland IN 46143 Zoning: GB Land Use: undeveloped land, parking Future Land Use: Mixed -use ~MNH 6 V-07-26 Base Map subject site 7 V-07-26 Base Map II 8 V-07-26 AERIAL 9 Proposed Plan of Operation, V-07-26 10 V-07-26 Petitioner’s Findings of Facts 11 12 6/11/2026 Members of the Johnson County Board of Zoning Appeals Re: V-07-26 Sandhu Properties INC 5362 Warrior Trail The Town of Whiteland (TOW) has been made aware of the request for a use variance for the property located at 5362 Warrior Trail, which is located in Johnson County. • Warrior Trail, which is owned by the Town of Whiteland, is only designated for 11,000 lbs and is not designated for truck traffic from 790’ north of Whiteland Rd. to the end of Warrior Trail. The road that was put into place for the neighboring parcel at 5440 Warrior Trail was regulated to have no more than 35 trucks. The road has been installed less than 18 months, and that portion of the road is already failing. With an already failing road, adding additional trucks will only add to the problem that has been created by the previous trucking development. See attached photos that were taken on June 9, 2026. • Stormwater. This site, since 2020 has increased impervious surface with no regards to any type of improvements on drainage. • IDEM/County Drainage Board/Municipal permits. As they have seemingly changed the overall layout of the property, have they ever obtained any permits for the improvements that have been made on this parcel? Have they ever reached out to the local jurisdiction for any type of official improvement or inquired about what would be required of them? • The TOW police department has made numerous interactions on this property, and it has created a nuisance in the general area due to exterior condition of the property. This has been a blighted property within our community since the parcel owner has taken ownership. • The increase in truck traffic and the impact that this type of development would have on TOW owned infrastructure would not outweigh the positives that would come from this parcel. They would undoubtedly utilize the existing structure as an “office” but would but would continue to utilize in the same condition and occupancy it currently as a multi-family structure. The Town of Whiteland is concerned that allowing this type of development would ultimately lead to more issues and resources being utilized by our staff than the positives that would come from this type of development where there is already a litany of viable options with parcels to the south to allow for trucking facilities and truck parking. We kindly request that this variance be denied, due to the state statute requirements for being granted a use variance based on IC 36-7-4-918.4 which requires: 1. “The approval will not be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community” - This would disproportionally represent the injurious portion to the Town of Whiteland as we have had multiple police resources and code enforcement regarding trash and rubbish in the area. Adding to the additional issues we’ve already seen with the neighboring parcel, this would only add additional trucks and usage on the TOW infrastructure. 2. “the strict application of the terms of zoning ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which the variance is sought” - Purchasing a property with an intent that 13 does not allow a permitted use of a zoned parcel does not constitute an “unnecessary hardship” rather a lack of planning on behalf of the parcel owner. Based off the Johnson County’s planning department definition within the current UDO states an “unnecessary hardship” Significant economic injury that: a. Arises from the strict application of zoning regulations in this ordinance to the conditions of a particular, existing parcel of property; b. Effectively deprives the parcel owner of all reasonable economic use of the parcel; and c. Is clearly more significant than compliance cost or practical difficulties. Furthermore, the existing structure doesn’t meet the setback requirements for GC zoning in the current UDO which requires front setbacks based off road designation (Collector/Local-40’, Minor Arterial-50’, I/Principal Arterial-60’). If the BZA does approve the use variance we would request the following commitments by the property owner: 1. Improve Warrior Trail with concrete from the Town limits to the end of Warrior Trail. The Town of Whiteland will be submitting for a Community Crossings Matching Grant program this Fall for reconstruction of Warrior Trail from Whiteland Rd to end of Town limits. This road will be converted to all concrete to ensure that it can withstand the truck traffic. 2. Apply for Town of Whiteland curb cut permit Sincerely, Carmen Young Billy Patrick Town Manager Building Commissioner Town of Whiteland Town of Whiteland Cc: Richard Hill, Whiteland Town Council President Derek Cox, Whiteland Town Marshal 14 Warrior Trail (Photos taken 6.9.2026) 15 16 Staff Report CASE NUMBER: V-12-26 ADDRESS: 3.9 acres located at approximately 3855 Olive Branch Road, Greenwood Parcel #: 41-04-11-022-022.000-038 PETITIONER: Story Custom Development LLC, By Eric Prime REQUEST VARIANCE OF USE of the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to allow a group home use for senior living (not permitted in an SR, Single Family Residential District) PROPERTY DESCRIPTION This 3.96-acre site is zoned SR (Single Family Residential). The property is currently unimproved grass and surrounded by mature trees and wooded areas. The property is surrounded by residential lots used residentially. Along the south, east, and west side of the property are platted major subdivisions, Brockton Manor and Highland Park. On the north side of Olive Branch Road are similar parcels of land used residentially. VARIANCE REQUEST This Use Variance request seeks approval to operate a residential group home specializing in senior memory care on the subject 3.96-acre tract. Because the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) does not explicitly permit group homes (defined under the UDO as “A non-profit or for-profit group home regulated under IC 31-27 for the sheltered care of persons with special needs, which, in addition to providing food and shelter, may also provide some combination of personal care, social or counseling services, and transportation.”) or nursing homes (defined under the UDO as “An establishment that provides continuous day and night room and board, personal services, and medical care for compensation, for two (2) or more elderly or infirm persons who are not related to the owner/operator of the home.”) as a permitted use within any unincorporated zoning district, a Use Variance is required to establish the use. Staff notes that this petition involves complex intersections between local zoning authority and federal protections of disabled individuals under the Fair Housing Amendments Act (FHAA) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Local jurisdictions are generally required to provide "reasonable accommodations" to afford persons with disabilities an equal opportunity to use and enjoy a residential dwelling and live in a residentially zoned district. However, recent Indiana trial court proceedings regarding similar facilities— specifically Willow Haven v. Carmel / Nagireddy out of Hamilton County—indicates that federal law does not completely bypass local administrative remedies. The Hamilton County Trial Court recently ruled that federal mandates do not require a municipality to dispense with its standard UDO definitions or enforcement without the petitioner first engaging in local variance procedures. Staff further notes the matter is currently pending with the Indiana Court of Appeals and therefore additional court guidance is not available. Accordingly, this petition is brought before the Johnson County Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) to formally consider whether the proposed use satisfies both Indiana statutory criteria for a use variance and the framework of a reasonable accommodation under federal law. Petitions Information: 17 The petitioner is proposing a one-story, residential-scale structure to operate as a senior memory care group home, and a detailed Plan of Operation and proposed site plan are attached to this report for further review. The facility will be constructed with standard residential architectural features to match the character of a single-family dwelling, featuring an interior layout of 12 bedrooms, 6 bathrooms, a single residential kitchen, and shared common living spaces. The facility will utilize private, on-site caregiver support to assist residents with daily living needs, though these caregivers will not provide clinical medical support. The structure will not include an attached garage, but the site plan designates 13 on-site parking spaces to accommodate staff, visitors, and support services. Regarding site conditions, a portion of the subject property falls within a FEMA-designated flood zone, but all proposed structural development will occur entirely outside of this area, with the only footprint inside the flood zone being the driveway. Additionally, the property contains several mature trees and established landscaping that currently provide an effective natural buffer between the site and the majority of the abutting residential lots. The petitioner plans to keep all of the trees that don’t need to be removed for the building pad and driveway. It is also anticipated to add more landscaping, primarily around the parking area and front yard. FINDINGS OF FACT: VARIANCE OF DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS State Requirement: The approval will not be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community. The proposed use is a residential facility serving senior citizens requiring memory care. In general, these facilities operate under quiet, low-impact conditions similar to standard residential uses. Provided that proper emergency vehicle access, life-safety compliance, and adequate utility capacities are verified, the residential nature of the care home is not likely to cause injury to public health or safety. State Requirement: The use and value of the area adjacent to the property included in the variance will not be affected in a substantially adverse manner. The proposed facility operates as a residential-scale memory care home, which inherently maintains a low- impact operational profile similar to standard single-family neighborhoods. Unlike commercial medical facilities, a small residential group home generates minimal traffic, structured delivery times, and quiet day-to- day operations. The facility will be constructed with similar residential elements which, along with the natural environment, will continue to influence the appearance of residential use to the adjacent areas. State Requirement: The need for the variance arises from some condition peculiar to the property involved. A distinct peculiarity exists within the broader context of the Johnson County zoning framework: the UDO lacks any zoning district where a group home or nursing home is allowed as a permitted use or right. Because the text of the UDO restricts this specific housing type globally across the county's jurisdiction, the terms of the zoning ordinance itself creates a unique regulatory hardship for this specific classification of property use and therefore a condition peculiar to the property involved. State Requirement: The strict application of the terms of the Zoning Ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which a variance is sought. Strict application of the UDO would entirely prohibit the petitioner from establishing a memory care home anywhere within the unincorporated county. Under federal law (the Fair Housing Act and Americans with Disabilities Act), individuals with cognitive disabilities such as dementia and Alzheimer's are afforded 18 protections that require local governments to make reasonable accommodations in their zoning rules. Completely barring this housing type constitutes an unnecessary hardship and presents significant federal compliance risk. State Requirement: The approval does not interfere substantially with the Comprehensive Plan. The Johnson County Comprehensive Plan generally seeks to preserve residential areas while ensuring diverse housing options exist for all segments of the population, including aging demographics and those with disabilities. While the Comprehensive Plan favors preserving the character of single-family areas, providing structured care for seniors within a residential environment aligns with broader community health goals, provided site-scale impacts are mitigated. Staff Recommendation: Staff recommends the following conditions if the Board makes a motion to approve this request: 1. The Plan of Operation shall be incorporated, including that the front façade of the proposed improvements and landscaping be substantially similar to Figure 1: Story Cottage at Williams Creek, Indianapolis. 2. The Petitioner shall take reasonable measures to preserve healthy mature trees located on the property that serve as a natural buffer between the proposed facility and adjacent properties. .GENERAL INFORMATION Applicant: Strand Associates INC 629 Washington Street Columbus IN 47601 Owner: Story Custom Development LLC 630 3rd Ave. SW Suite 200 Carmel IN 46032 Current Zoning: SR (single-family residential ) Existing Land Use: undeveloped Futu

Myers Representative County Council 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Ron Bates Alternate Member - County Council 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Greg Cantwell Surveyor - Office Held Office Term Shalee Bradley ANR County Extension Agent - Office Held Office Term Charles Canary Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2023 - 12/31/2027 Douglas Gray Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2024 - 12/31/2027 Steven Hickman Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2023 - 12/31/2027 Robert Page Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2024 - 12/31/2027 Stoney Vann Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2025 - 12/31/2028 UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT ORDINANCE – 2026 Amendment proposal The Department of Planning and Zoning has prepared a series of proposed text amendments to the Johnson County Uniﬁed Development Ordinance (UDO). Following the comprehensive adoption of the UDO in 2024, staff have identiﬁed several areas requiring technical cleanup, administrative clariﬁcation, and legislative updates. The proposed changes cover key operational areas including statutory protections for shooting ranges, deﬁned standards for event centers and group homes, clariﬁcation of accessory dwelling unit and structure sizes, and relief from suburban standards (such as sidewalks and individual lot landscaping) in rural and agricultural zoning districts.  Draft Redline Version of UDO Amendments as of 8-14-26  List of track changes to the UDO Below is the only amendment that was not voted on from the August meeting Group Home and Nursing Homes Rationale: Updates were made to the group home standards to align county zoning regulations better with ADA and federal fair housing guidelines, while resolving internal code inconsistencies across residential zoning districts. Deﬁnition & Scale: The UDO explicitly distinguishes a Group Home from larger institutional facilities, such as commercial nursing or convalescent centers. This distinction ensures group homes operate within a typical residential scale and character. State Compliance: Standards were updated to reference appropriate state licensing bodies—speciﬁcally the Division of Disability and Rehabilitative Services (DDRS) and the Division of Mental Health and Addiction (DMHA)—ensuring local oversight supports, rather than conﬂicts with, state licensing mandates. Permitted Districts & Occupancy Caps: Clariﬁed standards across residential and agricultural districts. Occupancy remains capped at eight (8) residents (excluding support staff) to maintain compatibility with single-family residential neighborhoods while ensuring compliance with federal Fair Housing Act protections for group living arrangements. Permitting & Review Process: Streamlined the review framework to clarify when a facility is permitted by right versus when it requires special approval, eliminating previous ambiguity surrounding unlisted uses or special exception requirements for state-licensed residential care homes. The purpose of this district is to provide for and protect substantial areas for a broad variety of agricultural uses where little or no urbanization has occurred or is planned to occur. The district intentionally limits broad residential uses to provide for large areas of contiguous farm land. b. Land Uses. A minimum lot size of two (2) acres shall be required for the use to locate on the property. 40.42. Recreational Vehicle Park and Campground. 239 GROUP HOME: A residential structure or facility where six (6) or more unrelated persons who are in need of care, support or supervision can live together, such as children or those who are elderly, disabled or mentally ill. Group Homes housing persons with developmental disabilities shall obtain, comply with, and maintain a license from the Indiana Division of Disability and Rehabilitative Services. Group Homes housing those living with psychiatric disorders or addictions shall obtain, comply with, and maintain a license from the Indiana Division of Mental Health and Addictions . A non-proﬁt or for- proﬁt group home regulated under IC 31-27 for the sheltered care of persons with special needs, which, in addition to providing food and shelter, may also provide some combination of personal care, social or counseling services, and transportation. GUARANTEE: Cash, bonds, or similar ﬁnancial instruments deposited with the County to ensure that required improvements will be constructed or installed. HEAVY EQUIPMENT SALES AND RENTALS: A business engaged in the rental or sales of powered heavy mechanical equipment. HEIGHT: The distance from the ground where the structure stands to the highest point of the structure. HOME BUSINESS: A lawful activity conducted for ﬁnancial gain, where such use does not include the sale of goods to customers on the premises or opening of the home to the public for the sale of goods or services without an invitation or appointment. The use diﬀers from a home occupation in that mechanical equipment related to the use may be stored outside of the building provided that proper screening is provided. Minimal traﬃc shall be required to occur on the property so that there is minimal disruption to the neighborhood. HOME OCCUPATION: An occupation, profession, domestic craft, or economic enterprise which is customarily conducted in a residential dwelling. The use diﬀers from a home business in that there shall be no outside indication that a business is operated on the site. HOMEOWNER’S ASSOCIATION: A formally constituted non-proﬁt association or corporation made up of the property owners and/or residents of a deﬁned area; who collectively may take permanent responsibility for costs and upkeep of commonly owned or designated community property. HOSPITAL / REHABILITATIVE CARE: An institution providing primary health services and medical or surgical care to persons, primarily inpatients, suﬀering from illness, disease, injury, disability, and other physical or mental conditions and including, as an integral part of the institution, related facilities, such as laboratories, outpatient facilities, training facilities, medical oﬃces, and staﬀ residences. This includes a clinic, hospital, or sanitarium, except a criminal, mental, or animal hospital; and nursing or convalescent home. HOTEL: A commercial building in which lodging is provided and oﬀered to the public for compensation. IMPROVEMENT LOCATION PERMIT (ILP): A certiﬁcate issued under this UDO permitting a person to erect, construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, improve, remove, convert, or demolish any building or structure within its jurisdiction or to change the use or condition of the land. 254 Appendix A, Land Use Matrix Residential Uses by Zoning District Table A.1, Land Use Matrix: Residential Uses -- = Prohibited; P = Permitted; US = Use Standards; SE = Special Exception Land Use Parks / Agricultural Residential Commercial Industrial PR AG AR SR DR MR MH GC HC IN Residential PR AG AR SR DR MR MH GC HC IN Single-Family Detached Dwelling -- P P P P P P -- -- -- Duplex (2 du) -- -- -- -- P P -- -- -- -- Townhouse (3 to 10 du) -- -- -- -- -- P -- SE -- -- Apartment (> 3 du) -- -- -- -- -- P -- SE -- -- Manufactured Home Park -- -- -- -- -- -- US -- -- -- Nursing Home P P Group Home SE SE SE SE US US Retirement Housing -- -- -- -- -- SE -- SE -- -- Residential Accessory PR AG AR SR DR MR MH GC HC IN Accessory Structure US US US US US US US US US US Accessory Dwelling Unit, Attached -- US US US -- -- -- -- -- -- Accessory Dwelling Unit, Detached -- US US US -- -- -- -- -- -- Commercial Uses of the Home PR AG AR SR DR MR

items.text: pg. 1 JOHNSON COUNTY Department of Planning & Zoning Phone: (317) 346-4350 86 West Court Street www.co.johnson.in.us Franklin, Indiana 46131 MEETING AGENDA Johnson County Advisory Plan Commission October 26th , 2026 - 6:00 PM Public Auditorium, West Annex Building 86 West Court Street, Franklin, Indiana CALL TO ORDER ROLL CALL APPROVAL of MINUTES Approval of minutes from the September 28th, 2026 meeting. OTHER APPOINTMENTS PUBLIC HEARINGS -CONTINUED HEARINGS- -NEW HEARINGS – P-1-26 RSBR E 300 S Road Commercial Subdivision Approval of RSBR E 300 S Road Preliminary Plat to create a 2-lot major commercial subdivision. Waiver from the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Chapter 6, Section K(4) & (5), to provide relief from public sanitary sewer and public water requirements. W-4-26 Sutton Waiver. 7106 S 300 W, Trafalgar Seeking a WAIVER of the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to permit a minor subdivision on a parent tract that has been altered since the adoption of the UDO. OLD BUSINESS NEW BUSINESS REPORTS and RECOMMENDATIONS pg. 2 ADJOURNMENT The next meeting of the Johnson County Advisory Plan Commission is scheduled for November 23rd, 2026 at 6:00 PM in the public auditorium of the Courthouse West Annex Building. LIVE STREAMING AVAILABLE HERE Meeting ID: 853 5483 6693 Passcode: 057410 (Link can also be found on the County Website under Events Calendar – Click on Events Website) In accordance with American Disabilities Act, any person attending the public meeting in need of reasonable accommodations in order to attend, hear, or present evidence at the public meeting on an agenda item should contact the Johnson County ADA coordinator, Barb Davis, at 86 W. Court St., Franklin, IN 46131, (317) 346-4329, bdavis@co.johnson.in.us. Pursuant to Indiana Code 5-14-9 (the “Act”), board member terms and appointing authority: Johnson County Plan Commission Appointment Member Appointing Authority Term Ron West Representative County Commissioner 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Jonathan T. Myers Representative County Council 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Ron Bates Alternate Member - County Council 1/1/2026 - 12/31/2026 Vincent Barr Appointed by Surveyor - Office Held Office Term Shalee Bradley DNR County Extension Agent - Office Held Office Term Charles Canary Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2023 - 12/31/2027 Douglas Gray Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2024 - 12/31/2027 Steven Hickman Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2023 - 12/31/2027 Robert Page Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2024 - 12/31/2027 Stoney Vann Citizen Member appointed by County Commissioners 1/1/2025 - 12/31/2028 Staff Report CASE NUMBER: P-1-26, RSBR E 300 S Road Commercial Subdivision ADDRESS: 3079 S US 31, Franklin PETITIONER: S&R Property LLP by Overland Engineering LLC REQUEST Primary Plat: Approval of the RSBR E 300 S Road Preliminary Plat to create a 2-lot major commercial subdivision. Waiver Request: Waiver from the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), Chapter 6, Section K(4) & (5), to provide relief from public sanitary sewer and public water requirements. STAFF RECOMMENDATION Staff recommends approval of this Major Plat and requested waivers PROPERTY DESCRIPTION This 5.23-acre parcel is located at the corner of Old US 31 and E 300 S, just south of the intersection of E 300 S and S US 31. The surrounding area is predominantly residential. The property formerly housed an agricultural sale barn and is currently used for storage by S&R Property LLC. PROPOSED PLAT If approved, this request will divide the 5.23-acre property into two (2) commercial lots: Lot 1 (North Lot): A 2.00-acre parcel intended for immediate commercial development, with vehicular access from E 300 S. Lot 2 (South Lot): A 2.72-acre parcel containing existing structures and operations, retaining vehicular access via the existing driveway on Old US 31. Prior Approvals & Actions: Previous Plat Review: This plat was previously considered for approval at this time last year. Minimum Lot Size Waiver: On February 23, 2026, the Plan Commission granted a waiver from Chapter 5, Section 3, Table 5.4 of the UDO to permit a commercial subdivision on a parcel under the 10-acre minimum requirement (5.23 acres). That subdivision standard has since been removed in the approved Unified Development Ordinance amendments presented in August 2026. GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS Technical Review Committee Reviewed on September 10, 2026. No additional comments were provided for this plat that differ from original review in 2025. The applicant has not conducted any additional traffic study other than the one provide with the petition last year dated 04/22/2024. At that time the Highway Department review the study and supplied comments as follow "Their study does assess the future traffic associated with the development and evaluated, but does not recommend, any dedicated turn lanes because no warrants were met. We have no additional comments.” - Daniel Johnston, P.E. | Highway Engineer A new traffic study is not warranted at this time. Johnson County Drainage Board Approved the drainage plan (DR 52-000-3596) on May 6, 2025. A confirmation letter is included in this packet verifying that the prior approval remains valid and no additional drainage review is required. Checkpoint Agencies: The Johnson County Planning Engineer, CenterPoint Energy, Johnson County Highway Department, Johnson County Health Department, Amity Community Volunteer Fire Department, and JCREMC have reviewed this petition and expressed no objections. WAIVER REQUEST & STAFF ANALYSIS The petitioner requests a waiver from the following infrastructure standards: 1. Public Sanitary Sewer (Chapter 6, Section K, Part 4): o Requirement: Major subdivisions must provide a complete sanitary sewer system connected to an approved public sanitary outlet. o Proposed Alternative: Because public sewer infrastructure is not available, the petitioner proposes an on-site commercial sewage system. Design and installation are subject to approval by the Indiana Department of Health under state commercial septic standards. 2. Public Water Facilities (Chapter 6, Section K, Part 5): o Requirement: Major subdivisions must connect to a public water supply when available within 300 feet of any boundary and provide a complete water delivery system including fire hydrants. o Proposed Alternative: Because the property lies outside a public water service district, the petitioner has already started approval process from IDEM for approval of a public well. A letter of Non-objection can be found in the exhibits. Staff Evaluation Findings:  Feasibility of Connection: Public water and sanitary sewer lines are not adjacent to or reasonably accessible from the subject site. Requiring utility extensions over this distance is cost-prohibitive and impractical based on current regional utility master plans.  Public Health & Environmental Protection: Commercial septic systems and public water wells fall under state regulatory oversight (IDH and IDNR). State design criteria ensure that environmental, health, and fire/potability safety standards are fully met.  Surrounding Context: The lack of municipal utility extensions in this immediate corridor makes private on-site commercial utilities standard for surrounding properties  The applicant is requesting a land division. The property is already zoned for commercial use and could be developed commercially using a private well and private septic system even without a land division. Because the property is large enough to accommodate additional development, the primary purpose of the land division is to establish clear, orderly property ownership and delineate individual responsibilities. Waiver Findings of Facts The granting of the waiver will not be detrimental to the public safety, health, or welfare or be injurious to nearby property The proposed commercial on-site sewage system will be designed, reviewed, and approved by the Indiana Department of Health (IDH) and local Health Department in accordance with state environmental and health standards. Additionally, the well system will be reviewed and approved by the Indiana Department of Natural Resources (IDNR). The waiver requested will not affect the area adjacent to the property in a substantially adverse manner because: Public sanitary sewer infrastructure is currently unavailable in the immediate vicinity of the property. All surrounding properties need to develop in the same fashion The conditions upon which the request for a waiver are based are unique to the property for which the waiver is sought and are not applicable generally to other properties. The subject property is located outside the service boundaries and geographic reach of municipal public sewer utilities. The physical absence of accessible public utility connections creates a unique constraint specific to this location that does not apply to properties within established utility service districts. Furthermore, while this property has been zoned commercial for some time, it predates the County's current policy goal requiring any newly established commercial land to be served by public infrastructure. The strict application of the terms of the Unified Development Ordinance will result in unnecessary hardship because: Strict application of the subdivision standards would force the applicant to extend public sewer lines over an excessive distance where municipal connection is unavailable. Although commercial development could proceed on the unified property utilizing a state-regulated septic system without seeking a land division, strict enforcement of the subdivision rules makes dividing the tract impossible, despite the site's complete suitability for on-site utilities. The waiver is not primarily for the economic benefit of the petitioner because: The request stems from the physical absence and unavailability of public sanitary sewer infrastructure adjacent to the site, rather than a desire to reduce development costs. T The waiver request is not due to a hardship caused by the current owner of the property. The lack of public sewer infrastructure serving this geographical location is an existing environmental and municipal service condition created by regional utility distribution boundaries, not by any action, plan, or development decision made by the property owner. The waiver will not, in any manner, contravene provisions of the Zoning Ordinance, Comprehensive Plan, or Official Map, as interpreted by the Commission. While the future land use map designates the area as Rural Residential, the property has a long- established commercial history (formerly agricultural sales and current commercial storage) and holds proper commercial zoning. Granting a utility waiver under state health oversight fulfills the ordinance’s core objective—ensuring safe and adequate sanitation—without expanding the commercial footprint or conflicting with the broader goals of the Comprehensive Plan, as the intended use remains consistent with the site's established operational history. GENERAL INFORMATION Applicant: Overland Engineering LLC Owner: S & R PROPERTY LLP 5144 Madison Ave Ste 11 Indianapolis, IN 46227 Area: 5.23 acres Current Zoning: GC (General Commercial) Existing Land Use: Warehouse/Storage Comprehensive Plan: Rural Residential -MNH P-1-26 Base Map subject site P-1-26 Base Map II – 5 acre parent tract P-1-26 Aerial Map https://maps.app.goo.gl/ejf5qBEwvda694Kq8 - Google Street View P-1-26 Petitioner’s Findings of Facts for Waiver Archived: Friday, May 15, 2026 10:34:17 AM From: Cantwell Gregg - Surveyor Mail received time: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 18:41:34 +0000 Subject: RE: Fwd: RSBS E 300 S Road - Primary Commerciail Subdivision Recommendation Letter Re: DR 52-000-3596 Rodney Parrott PE Overland Engineering LLC Rodney Yes, DR 52-000-3596 (Preliminary Plat) was approved as filed, at the May 6th, 2025 Johnson County Drainage Board Meeting. All approvals have a two year approval window. Please contact this office if you have any further questions regarding the above approval. Thank you, J Gregg Cantwell, IWLA | Surveyor Johnson County Government (317) 346-4341 gcantwell@JohnsonCounty.in.gov JohnsonCounty.in.gov 86 W. Court St. Franklin, IN, 46131 From: Rodney Parrott <rodney@overlandeng.com> Sent: Monday, April 20, 2026 8:31 AM To: Cantwell Gregg - Surveyor <gcantwell@co.johnson.in.us> Subject: Re: Fwd: RSBS E 300 S Road - Primary Commerciail Subdivision Recommendation Letter Greg, Did you get a chance to review this one? The planning office wants to be sure your OK with it and then we can resubmit for the plat (no drainage changes). Thank you. Rodney Parrott PE Overland Engineering LLC 1598 Imperial Ctr. Suite 2009 West Plains, MO 65775 417-256-8150 (office) On 4/7/2026 3:03 PM, Rodney Parrott wrote: Greg, Per our conversation, attached is the previous Drainage Board approval letter from 5/6/25. If still acceptable, we will move forward with the replat (now that we have the 2 acre waiver vs. the 10 acres) Thank you. Rodney Parrott PE Overland Engineering LLC 1598 Imperial Ctr. Suite 2009 West Plains, MO 65775 417-256-8150 (office) -------- Forwarded Message -------- Subject:RSBS E 300 S Road - Primary Commerciail Subdivision Recommendation Letter Date:Tue, 6 May 2025 17:19:52 +0000 From:Hoover Richard - Planning & Zoning <rhoover@JohnsonCounty.in.gov> To:Rodney Parrott <rodney@overlandeng.com> Rodney, Please see attached.3 Thanks, Dik Richard R. Hoover | Planning Engineer Johnson County Government (317) 346-4350 rhoover@JohnsonCounty.in.gov JohnsonCounty.in.gov 86 W. Court St. Franklin, IN, 46131 INDIANA DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT 100 N. Senate Avenue • Indianapolis, IN 46204 (800) 451-6027 • (317) 232-8603 • Fax (317) 233-6647 • www.idem.IN.gov Mike Braun Clint Woods Governor Commissione r June 23, 2026 Mr. Rodney Parrot Dollar General-Amity 1598 Imperial Ctr. Suite 2009 West Plains, MO 65775 Dear Mr. Parrot: Re: Letter of Non-Objection—Well 1 Dollar General-Amity PWSID #: IN2410905 Mr. Thomas Wiseman of this office conducted a well site survey on June 3, 2026, at Dollar General- Amity, Johnson County; Franklin, Indiana. All information has been received and the enclosed survey has been issued. The survey is valid for one (1) year from the date of the survey. A copy has been forwarded to the Construction Permit Section of the Drinking Water Branch. If you have any questions regarding this correspondence, please contact Thomas Wiseman of my staff at TWiseman@idem.in.gov or by calling (317) 471-7833. You may also contact Lucio Ternieden by email at LTernied@idem.IN.gov or by phone at 317- 234-7461. S i n c e r e l y , Lucio M. Ternieden, Chief Field Inspection Section D r i n k i n g W a t e r B r a n c h Office of Water Quality Enclosure Cc: Johnson County Health Department Liz Melvin, IDEM Construction Permits Jean Kocher, IDEM Construction Permits REPORT OF SURVEY Letter of Non-Objection to Well Site Dollar General- Amity PWSID # IN2410905 LOCATION: Blue River Township, Johnson County, Indiana SURVEYED BY: Thomas Wiseman, In diana Department of Environmental Management SURVEY DATE: June 3, 2026 GENERAL: A sanitary well site survey was conducted for an existing production well. The well will be named WL001 – Well 1, a 6 inch PVC cased well with a proposed pump capacity of approximately 10gpm. GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF WELL SITE: The well site is located adjacent to the parking lot of the former Johnson County Sale Pavilion. Water from this well when completed will feed the proposed Dollar General- Amity store. COMMENTS: The proposed well is an exis ting production well that will serve the Dollar General- Amity. There are a few sources of contamination within one thousand (1000) feet of the proposed location. The proposed well location covered in this report was surveyed from the standpoint of providing protection from sources of contamination originating at or near the ground surface in the vicinity of the proposed well. CONDITIONS OF OPERATION: The proposed well location complies with 327 IAC 8-3.4-9 and once permitted and installed may serve the Dollar General- Amity Transient public water supply subject to the following conditions. 1. That the Dollar General- Amit y public water supply system control the area within one hundred (100) feet from the well by, purchase, registered easement, long-term lease, or by covenants in the deeds of the surrounding land, prohibiting the construction or maintenance of any sewers, drains, privies, cesspools, septic tanks, or any other potential source of contamination within one hundred (100) feet of the wells. Copies of these documents are to be provided to this office. 2. That the Dollar General- Amit y public water supply system submits to this office a complete report on each well drilled. This report should include a log showing the different strata encountered and the depth of the pump setting, the length of the screen, the static and pumping water levels, pumping capacity, log of pump test, back-grouting, and details of how the well casing is sealed into rock, if rock is encountered. Copies of the report shall be maintained on site. 3. That complete plans and specifications for the construction of the well and pumphouse, and treatment equipment, connecting piping, sampling spigots, and other pertinent information be certified according to 327 IAC 8-3.4-3 and submitted to the Permits Section, Drinking Water Branch of IDEM for review and approval. 4. That the system be equippe d with a sampling tap for raw water from the well. Sampling taps shall be of the smooth nosed type without interior or exterior threads, shall not be of the mixing type, and shall not have a screen, aerator, or other such appurtenance. The tap is to be located directly after the well, before any branches to storage/pressure tanks and any treatment. The sample tap is to comply with the requirements of the ground water rule. 5. A well site review of the property in the standpoint of Groundwater Under Direct Influence (GWUDI) indicated that at this time no further action or raw water sampling for bacteria is needed to determine GWUDI. Should the well yield positive samples, further determination by this office may be required 6. That after the well has been chlorinated and allowed to rest for at least twelve (12) hours and pumped to waste for a minimum of fifteen (15) minutes with no detectable chlorine residual, two (2) consecutive samples shall be collected in accordance with AWWA Standard C654 not less than thirty (30) minutes apart from each new well and be tested for coliform bacteria by a certified laboratory and shall all confirm that the water in the well is acceptable before the well is placed in service. The system also has the option to take two (2) consecutively satisfactory bacteriological samples at least twenty-four (24) hours apart to confirm the water in the well is acceptable before placing the well into service. Copies of the sample results are to be mailed to Thomas Wiseman, Field Inspection Section, of the Drinking Water Branch and submitted to the Drinking Water Branch’s Permits Section at dwpermits@idem.in.gov. 7. That one (1) satisfactory ni trate sample, and one (1) fluoride sample be taken from each well before the wells are put into production. Copies of the sample results are to be mailed to Thomas Wiseman, Field Inspection Section, of the Drinking Water Branch and submitted to the Drinking Water Branch’s Permits Section at dwpermits@idem.in.gov. 8. That the area immediately su rrounding the well casings be sloped, so that surface water drains away and prevent any water from pooling or standing next to the casing. 9. That in accordance with 327 IAC 8-3.4-16(a)(5)(A)(ii) the permanent well casing shall terminate at a level of at least eighteen (18) inches above finished grade or at least thirty-six (36) inches above the regulatory flood elevation if located in a designated flood hazard area identified by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). 10. That original well logs and c opies of well production tests are submitted to the Division of Water, Department of Natural Resources in accordance with IC 25-39-4 within thirty (30) days after completion. Copies of the logs and tests shall be maintained on site. 11. That all chemical application to the grounds surrounding the well sites comply with label directions and in conformance with rules of the Indiana Office of the State Chemist and Indiana Administrative Code (IAC) at 355 IAC as applicable, 357 IAC as applicable and 327 IAC 8-3.4-9. 12. That storm or sanitary sewers , including field drain tiles, shall not be located within the isolation area of a production well unless constructed according to 327 IAC 8-3.4-9(5)(B). 13. That the well be cased to at least fifty (50) feet below ground surface in accordance with 327 IAC 8-3.4-20 for rotary well drilling and 327 IAC 8-3.4-21 for cable tool well drilling, unless otherwise approved by the commissioner as per 327 IAC 8- 3.4-27. 14. A review of the IDEM’s Offi ce of Land Quality records show that the proposed well location is not within two hundred (200) feet of a known Environmental Restrictive Covenant (ERC) property boundary. 15. This well site survey shall be valid for a period of one (1) year ending June 3, 2027. If construction has not begun by June 3, 2027, a request for an updated well site survey or an extension of this survey must be made prior to beginning construction. 16. This well site survey approval is only valid for the location that is noted in this survey. If IDEM issues a construction permit for this project, these conditions will be incorporated into the construction permit. This survey does not constitute a construction permit. You must obtain a valid construction permit prior to construction. If your construction application has not yet been submitted, you must include a copy of this survey as a part of a complete construction permit application. SENSITIVE INFORMATION NOT FOR PUBLIC DISCLOSURE LOCATION OF WELL SITE: The well is located adjac ent to the parking area of the former Johnson County Sale Pavilion. GPS Location: N 39.4335333333, E -86.0061388889 PLSS: Township 11N, Range 5E, Section 5 Blue River Township, Johnson County, Indiana Potential Sources of Contamination: There ar e a few potential sources of contamination within the sanitary setback radius of the proposed well: 1. Bathrooms in the existing building 110’ to the N 2. Proposed septic system 200' to the N 3. Railroad runs 200' to the E 4. Old US 31 runs 300' to the W 5. E CR 300 S runs 500' to the N 6. US 31 runs 500' to the W 7. Agricultural fields starting at 700' to the NE and SW Johnson County Health Department 95 S. Drake Rd., Franklin, IN 46131 Phone: (317) 346-4365, Fax: (317) 736-5264 P:\SEPTIC PROGRAM\COMMERCIAL SEPTICS\Dollar Gerneral at Spartan 3079 US 31 sout\20260729_let RE Soil Report Expectations.dotx July 29, 2026 S & R PROPERTY LLP 5144 Madison Ave Ste 11 Indianapolis, IN 46227 RE: Soil Report Expectations 3079 S US 31 41-12-05-022-003.000-004 FRANKLIN IN 46131 Dear S & R PROPERTY LLP, The Johnson County Health Department is contacting you regarding the issuance of the septic system installation permit for the Amity Dollar General. This letter is based upong the existing soil report from Glacier’s Edge Soil Consulting, dated 6/19/2024. There are two issues at this site, one is compaction, and the other is fill soil. The compaction will be remediated by plowing the site for the elevated system. The plans should specify that the site must be plowed to a minimum depth of 13 inches (two inches below compaction). This plow depth is based on current site and soil conditions. This will change after the fill is removed, which is the second issue. There is 6 inches of fill at soil boring 2 and 4 inches of fill at soil boring 3. It is the fill that must be removed. The plan will need to show how this fill can be removed without creating a depression and provide instructions for fill removal. The plans may provide existing and proposed contour to indicate that there will not be a depression when the fill is removed. As part of the system construction the fill will be removed. An additional on-site soil evaluation will be preformed to show the fill has been removed and describe new depths of compaction, limiting layer and seasonal high water table. After the fill is removed, the limiting layer must still be at least 20 inches below grade and soil compaction cannot exceed 12 inches for the site to be considered suitable. After the fill has been removed, then the compaction will be remediated two inches below the new compaction depth as described by the soil scientist. Example: The compaction is now 11 inches deep, if 4-6 inches of the compaction gets removed then it may only be 5-7 inches
