All unauthorized materials and activities have been removed from the site, the house has been secured and boarded up, and access points have been blocked to prevent further unauthorized use. The property has remained in full compliance with the Board’s motion and applicable zoning regulations since the June Board of Zoning Appeals meeting. This petition was previously continued by the Board to allow the petitioner time to demonstrate active efforts to abate all unpermitted uses prior to formal approval. Aside from the site cleanup and securing of the property, no other changes or modifications have been submitted regarding the application. All other findings, details, and recommendations in the original Staff Report remain unchanged REQUEST VARIANCE OF USE of the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to allow for a trucking parking and trucking facility business (not permitted in a GB-zoned property). PROPERTY DESCRIPTION This variance request involves a 12.696-acre parcel zoned GB (General Business). The property is currently unimproved, though it contains an existing dwelling that is not being used for residential purposes. The land is currently being utilized for parking. Surrounding land uses include: South: Several semi-tractor oriented businesses. North: Semi Parking, Warehouse, and manufacturing uses, including a similar use approved in 2023 by the Board of Zoning Appeals. All affected parcels, with the exception of 5440 Warrior Trail, are located within the Town of Whiteland limits VARIANCE OF USE REQUEST If approved, this Variance of Use request would allow the property to be redeveloped as a commercial truck parking lot, with the potential to repurpose the existing structure for fleet operations. Proposed Site Plan & Operations Parking Capacity: The submitted site plan proposes parking for approximately 71 semi-trucks and semi-trailers. Structure Reuse: The existing structure is proposed to be converted into an office building. Technical Review Adjustments: The final number of parking spots may be reduced during the Technical Review Committee (TRC) review of the civil plans to ensure compliance with development standards, including parking lot setbacks, landscaping, and drainage requirements. Hours of Operation: According to the petitioner’s submitted Plan of Operation, the facility will operate 24 hours a day with security. REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS The development will be required to go through the Technical Review Committee process and must adhere to the following:  All commercial standards in the zoning ordinance.  Procurement of a State Design Release for commercial use of the existing building.  Full compliance with all requirements of the Stormwater Management Ordinance. STAFF NOTES AND RECOMMENDATION This property has been continuously used for truck parking without authorization from staff, despite repeated enforcement notices from the department. However, staff notes that this formal application indicates the property owners are now making an effort to correct past violations and establish a compliant parking facility. If approved, this process will ensure the development is better suited for the area in both appearance and operational use. The existing dwelling on the property has previously been used by the property owner and guests as a social gathering spot, which has presented ongoing issues for the Town of Whiteland. The house is currently unfit for occupation. This unauthorized use must cease immediately, regardless of the outcome of this variance request. The Town of Whiteland has provided an official response to this use request, which is attached to this staff report for review. The requested variance is consistent with and similar to the uses of adjoining properties. Staff recommends the following conditions for consideration: 1. Required Approvals: The development must obtain all required permits and approvals before any improvements are made to the property. 2. Cease Existing Operations: All current semi-truck parking on the property must be removed until proper permits have been issued and site improvements are completed. 3. Structure Occupancy: The existing structure cannot be occupied or used until proper commercial permits have been obtained. 4. Nuisance Mitigation: If the structure is not brought into commercial use within one (1) year of this approval, it must be demolished and removed from the property to deter improper use and prevent a public nuisance. 5. Town Interlocal Agreement: The development must include and adhere to all stipulations provided by the Town of Whiteland. STAFF VARIANCE OF USE FINDINGS OF FACT: STAFF ANALYSIS 1. The approval will not be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community. The proposed conversion of the property into a secure, 24-hour commercial semi-truck parking facility will not be injurious to the public health, safety, or general welfare, provided all staff conditions are met. The property will undergo a rigorous Technical Review Committee (TRC) process to ensure proper drainage, stormwater management, landscaping, and setbacks are implemented. Furthermore, requiring the unapproved, hazardous use of the existing residential structure to cease and mandating its removal if not developed within one year directly mitigates an existing public nuisance and improves community safety. 2. The use and value of the area adjacent to the property included in the variance will not be affected in a substantially adverse manner. The proposed use is highly consistent with the established character of the immediate area. The property is bordered to the south and north by semi-tractor-oriented businesses. By bringing this site into compliance through formal development standards, the physical appearance and operational safety of the site will be significantly upgraded compared to its current unauthorized state, thereby protecting adjacent property values. 3. The need for the variance does arise from some condition peculiar to the property involved. The 12.696-acre parcel is currently zoned GB (General Business), which does not permit the transportation and logistics support uses that have become dominant in this immediate area. Due to the intense semi-tractor traffic and industrial warehouse operations directly bordering the site to the north and south, it is highly impractical for this property to be developed for any of the retail or light commercial uses standardly permitted in the GB district. The unique physical location of the parcel—effectively locked within a heavy industrial and transportation corridor—creates a distinct peculiarity where standard general business uses are no longer viable or compatible. 4. The strict application of the terms of the Zoning Ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which variance is sought. Strict adherence to the GB zoning text would restrict the property from fulfilling its most logical economic use as a support facility for the surrounding transport sector. Forcing standard retail or office development on a site locked between semi-truck facilities and manufacturing warehouses creates an unnecessary hardship, as such businesses would struggle with compatibility. Granting the variance allows the petitioner to formalize and legally rectify the land use in a way that matches the market reality of the corridor. 5. The approval does not interfere substantially with the Comprehensive Plan. The Comprehensive Plan’s recommendation for mixed use in this area. Mixed uses development is intended to encourage a well-planned, integrated mix of compatible uses that relate well and support one another. This use is compatible with other uses in the area. GENERAL INFORMATION Applicant: Chad Leinart 3200 Sycamore Ct, Ste 2A Columbus IN 47203 Owner: Sandhu Properties Inc 5362 Warrior Trl Whiteland IN 46143 Zoning: GB Land Use: undeveloped land, parking Future Land Use: Mixed -use ~MNH V-07-26 Base Map subject site V-07-26 Base Map II V-07-26 AERIAL Proposed Plan of Operation, V-07-26 V-07-26 Petitioner’s Findings of Facts Staff Report CASE NUMBER: V-16-26 ADDRESS: 5440 Warrior Trail, Whiteland PETITIONER: Shana Property LLC by Chris Duke ADDENDUM FOR OCTOBER BOARD MEETING The applicant is meeting with the town of Whiteland on October 22, 2026. Update will be provided at Board meeting. REQUEST Approval to modify a site plan and Plan of Operation of an approved Use Variance (V-12-23) Variance of Use of the Johnson County Zoning Ordinance to allow for a trucking company business (not permitted in a GB-zoned property). PROPERTY DESCRIPTION This variance request involves a 7.31-acre parcel that is zoned GB (General Commercial District). To the south are several semi-tractor-oriented businesses and to the north are warehouse/manufacturer uses. All parcels are within the Town of Whiteland limits. MODIFICATIONS TO A USE VARIANCE In December 2023, the property received approval for Use Variance V-12-23 to operate a trucking business. A subsequent modification to the Site Plan and Plan of Operation was approved in June of 2025. The petitioner is now requesting further modifications to the Plan of Operation and Site Plan to accommodate an intensification of the use. The revised site plan includes an additional 54 semi- truck or trailer parking spaces, bringing the site's total capacity to 89 parking spots compared to the original approval. STAFF VARIANCE OF USE FINDINGS OF FACT: STAFF ANALYSIS 1. The approval will not be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community. The proposed expansion of semi-truck and trailer parking (adding 54 spaces for a total of 89 spaces) will not impair public health, safety, or general welfare. 2. The use and value of the area adjacent to the property included in the variance will not be affected in a substantially adverse manner. The intensification of the trucking operation is compatible with the surrounding land-use context, which includes adjacent semi-tractor operations directly to the south and warehouse/manufacturing uses to the north. Because the expanded parking footprint aligns with the established commercial and industrial character of the corridor, it is unlikely to adversely affect surrounding property values. 3. The need for the variance does arise from some condition peculiar to the property involved. The property is a 7.31-acre site zoned GB surrounded by land uses within Whiteland municipal limits that are predominantly heavy commercial, logistics, and industrial in nature. The underlying GB zoning designation does not reflect the dominant semi-tractor and logistics character established on adjacent properties in the immediate vicinity. 4. The strict application of the terms of the Zoning Ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which variance is sought. Strict enforcement of GB zoning standards would prohibit the expansion of an already established and previously approved trucking business on a parcel suited for heavy vehicle logistics. Denying the site plan and plan of operation modification would unreasonably restrict the site's functional utility and prevent the business from adapting to documented operational demand within a commercial/industrial corridor. 5. The approval does not interfere substantially with the Comprehensive Plan. the Comprehensive Plan designates this area for mixed-use development, which encourages a well-planned, integrated combination of compatible land uses that support surrounding commercial and industrial activity. GENERAL INFORMATION Applicant: Chris Duke 3567 E 700 N Whiteland, IN 46184 Owner: Shana Property LLC 2947 Hearthside Dr. Greenwood, IN 46173 Zoning: GB Land Use: undeveloped land, parking Future Land Use: Mixed- Use ~MNH~ V-16-26 Base Map subject site V-16-26 Base Map II V-16-26 AERIAL V-16-25 Original Approved Site Plan Modified Site Plan in 2025 V-16-26, 2025 PLAN OF OPERATION V-16-26 Petitioner’s Findings of Facts Staff Report CASE NUMBER: V-18-26 ADDRESS: 5510 Rocklane Road, Greenwood Parcel # 41-06-05-012-004.000-006 PETITIONER: Prabhdeep Chahal, By Badger Engineering REQUEST VARIANCE OF USE from the Johnson County Unified Development Ordinance to permit a wedding and event venue, which is not a permitted use in the SR (Single-Family Residential) zoning district. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION This 3.99-acre site is zoned SR (Single-Family Residential) and is improved with a single-family dwelling and an in-ground pool. The site is surrounded by parcels of similar size or larger, featuring single-family dwellings and heavily wooded areas. VARIANCE OF USE If approved, this request would allow the subject property to be used as a wedding and event venue. The submitted Plan of Operation indicates that the venue would be available for rent seven days a week, with the following hours of operation: Sunday through Thursday: 9:00 AM to 11:00 PM Friday and Saturday: 9:00 AM to 12:00 AM (Midnight) Staffing: Up to four staff members per event. The applicant intends to use the garage area of the existing dwelling for events, while the main dwelling space will remain strictly for residential use and will not be part of the event space. Patrons will be permitted to utilize the outdoor grounds and pool area. The applicant has provided conceptual plans for a future parking area. No new primary structures will be constructed for this use, though a building addition will be added to accommodate restrooms. The venue is designed to accommodate up to 200 guests. Remodeling of the current barn and construction of the new restroom addition will require a State Design Release and County commercial building permits. No Development Standard Variances are requested at this time, as the petitioner wishes to secure land use approval prior to committing resources to civil engineering drawings. STAFF ANALYSIS & FINDINGS Per the Zoning Ordinance, the purpose of the SR District is to accommodate single-family residential uses. In addition, the Comprehensive Plan encourages the preservation and protection of the rural character and agricultural tradition of Johnson County. The introduction of a commercial event venue accommodating up to 200 guests creates significant compatibility concerns with the surrounding residential neighborhood: Noise Impacts: Noise generated by vehicles, crowds, amplified music, and general venue activities— particularly during late-evening hours—would negatively impact the use and enjoyment of nearby residential properties. There are approximately 22 dwellings located within a quarter-mile of this property, and this figure does not include the numerous additional residences situated just outside that quarter-mile range. These properties are well within range to hear noise generated from the venue, including music played from inside a building. Character Compatibility: A large-scale commercial operation of this intensity directly conflicts with the low-density, rural residential character of the area. While staff understands the convenience and economic potential this variance might afford the petitioner, staff ultimately asserts that the required legal findings cannot be met and that a wedding and event center is not appropriate for this residential site. FINDINGS OF FACT: VARIANCE OF USE 1. The approval will be injurious to the public health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community. While required improvement permits from applicable regulatory agencies (such as building and health permits) would precede site development, the intense operational characteristics of a commercial event venue in a residential neighborhood present potential impacts on community welfare regarding safety, traffic, and peace. 2. The use and value of the area adjacent to the property included in the variance will be affected in a substantially adverse manner. The use and value of adjacent properties will be affected in a substantially adverse manner. Noise generated by vehicles, crowds, amplified music, and general venue activities—particularly during late-evening hours—would negatively impact the use and enjoyment of nearby residential properties. There are approximately 22 dwellings located within a quarter-mile of this property (not counting numerous additional residences situated just outside that range), and these nearby homes are well within range to hear noise generated from the venue, including music played from inside a building. Furthermore, the introduction of up to 200 guests and associated traffic arriving and departing would deviate significantly from the quiet, low-density residential character of the area. 3. The need for the variance does arise from some condition peculiar to the property involved. There is no obvious condition particular to the property that prevents its use for permitted residential purposes or that supports introducing a commercial event venue into a single-family residential zone. 4. The strict application of the terms of the Zoning Ordinance will constitute an unnecessary hardship if applied to the property for which variance is sought. Strict application of the terms of the UDO does not constitute an unnecessary hardship, as the property is currently improved with a single-family residence and an in-ground pool, and can fully and successfully accommodate a residential use in compliance with the SR (Single-Family Residential) zoning district. 5. The approval does interfere substantially with the Comprehensive Plan. The approval would interfere substantially with the Comprehensive Plan and the underlying intent of the SR Zoning District, which is designed to accommodate single-family residential uses. Additionally, the Future Land Use map designates the area for rural/agricultural preservation, and the introduction of a large-scale commercial event venue accommodating up to 200 guests does not align with the rural residential character or traditional land use patterns of the area. GENERAL INFORMATION Applicant: Prabhdeep Chahal 5846 Cherokee Drive Bargersville IN 46106 Owner: Hadley Mason 5510 Rocklane Road Greenwood IN Zoning: SR (Single Family Residential) Land Use: Residential Future Land Use: Agricultural -MNH V-18-26 BASE MAP Subject Site V-18-26 BASE MAP II

items.title: Council Minutes 3-9-2026
items.text: COUNTY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING —MARCH 9, 2026 The meeting was called to order by Council President, Michele Ann Graves. A. Call the Meeting to Order 1. Roll Call The following members were present: Jonathan Myers, John Mailers, Pamela Burton, John Ditmers, and Ron Bates. Melinda Griesemer was absent. 2. Invocation Mrs. Burton gave the invocation. 3. Pledge of Allegiance Mrs. Graves led the Pledge of Allegiance. 4. Approval of 3/9/26 Agenda Mrs. Graves stated the two following changes to the agenda: 1. Remove item C9 General Fund (#1001-0159)Comm Corr/Adult 2. Item C7d should be 1123.11453.00000.0220 -Supp-Asst Director Mr. Bates made a motion to approve the agenda as amended. Mr. Ditmars seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. 5. Public Comments (agenda items only, limited to 5 minutes per person) There were no public comments. B. Routine Matters - Consent Agenda By a single motion, the Board approves the following items, which may include Salary Ordinance Amendments, Additional Appropriations, Reductions, and Transfers. Any items listed on the consent agenda may be removed by a Council member and moved to the regular agenda. Mr. Myers made a motion to approve the consent agenda as presented. Mr. Mallers seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. I. Approval of 2/9/26 Regular Meeting Minutes 2. 93.069 CRI BP2 2025-2026 (#8228) Health (a) From: 8228.36200.00000.0210 Communications $ (720.00) To: 8228.42000.00000.0210 Operating Equipment $ 320.00 To: 8228.25801.00000.0210 Food (new) $ 400.00 3. Park Non-Reverting Capital Improv (#1178) Park (a) AA: 1178.42001.00000.0271 Building & Land Improvement $ 265,746.00 4. Park Non-Reverting Operating (#1179) Park (a) AA: 1179.42001.00000.0273 Building & Land Improvement $ 225,000.00 5. Phelps Charitable Fund (#4113) Park (a) AA: 4113.42000.00000.0128 Operating Equipment $ 15,307.85 (b) AA: 4113.32001.00000.0128 Promotional (new) $ 2,122.37 Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 1 of 12 6. VASIA 2026 (#9129) VASIA (a) AA: 9129.32000.00000.0133 Dues & Subscriptions $ 2,000.00 (b) AA: 9129.36102.00000.0133 Contractual Services $ 59,210.00 (c) AA: 9129.25801.00000.0133 Food $ 2,100.00 (d) AA: 9129.21001.00000.0133 Volunteer Favors $ 2,000.00 (e) AA: 9129.31500.00000.0133 Travel & Training $ 4,690.00 7. Enhanced Access (#1154) Recorder (a) AA: 1154.36102.00000.0104 Contractual Services $ 1,750.00 8. Prosecutor Hub Grant 2024-2025 (#9133) Prosecutor (a) AA: 9133.14200.00000.0108 Fica-Social Security 166.91 (b) AA: 9133.14300.00000.0108 PERF 251.38 (c) AA: 9133.19900.00000.0108 Overtime $ 2,182.31 (d) AA: 9133.19500.00000.0108 Grant Reimb for Personnel $ 256.71 9. Prosecutor Hub Grant 2026 (#9164) Prosecutor (a) AA: 9164.14200.00000.0108 Fica-Social Security $ 1,530.00 (b) AA: 9164.14300.00000.0108 PERF $ 2,240.00 (c) AA: 9164.19900.00000.0108 Overtime $ 16,230.00 10. Grants Awarded/Non-Governmental (#4300-0155) Sheriff (a) AA: 4300.31500.00000.0155 Travel & Training $ 2,602.00 C. Salary Ordinance Amendments, Additional Appropriations, Reductions, and Transfers 1. Pretrial Diversion Program (#2509) Prosecutor Michelle Murray, Office Administrator, was present to request an additional appropriation to close this grant out. Mrs. Graves asked if this is needed due to overspending the grant. Mrs. Murray replied, she doesn't think it was overspending but isn't sure since it was prior to her time; she just knows this is needed to close out the grant. Mrs. Graves noted the request letter stated it was to correct a negative balance in this fund. She then asked if there were precautions in place to prevent grant funds from running in the red moving forward. Mrs. Murray stated they are trying to make revisions as they go and make corrections as they see them. Mr. Ditmars made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mr. Bates seconded the motion, which carried unanimously. (la) AA: 2509.30060.00000.0286 Grant Adjustments $ 1,032.53 Mrs. Murray was also present to request a part-time hourly rate to $26.50 for a part-time paralegal, which equals the same hourly rate of their full-time paralegals. She noted they would like to hire a part-time person, who has paralegal experience to work in their Pretrial Diversion programs. Mrs. Burton asked what was the maximum they budgeted at budget time and if this amount was over what they initially said their margins would be. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 2 of 12 Mrs. Murray answered, yes, they initially budgeted $25.00/hr. Mrs. Burton then stated this would be new money then, an adjustment to the actual budget. Mrs. Murray replied yes; however, right now they are not asking for any additional appropriations in this specific line item. Mrs. Graves noted she did a little bit of research. In 2025, they budgeted $36,000 in this line item and spent $30,347. In 2026, $36,000 was budgeted again; she then asked if it is anticipated to need more money in this line item due to hiring this additional part time person. Mrs. Murray replied she hoped not; this person will be only working two days a week, and not every week. Mrs. Graves stated that Council prefers these types of requests be made at budget time and inquired why this one got overlooked. Mrs. Murray explained they were unaware at budget time they needed help in this area; however, due to some turnover of employees, they are trying to fill this position with part time help instead of full time. Mr. Myers asked why they need help in this area at this increased rate. Mrs. Murry answered by hiring someone with prior paralegal experience, saves them a lot of time training. They are behind due to the volume of cases they have. Mrs. Graves stated that Council would like to see part time job descriptions; she would like those sent to Taylor Webster, Assistant County Attorney for review. Mr. Mallers made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mr. Myers seconded the motion, which carried 5-1; Mrs. Burton voted nay. (1 b) 2509.11400.00000.0286 — Part Time — request approval to increase part time rate from $25.00 to $26.50 2. General Fund (#1001-0201) Highway 3. LIT Economic Development (#1112-0201) Highway Luke Mastin, Supervisor, was present for several requests. Mr. Mastin stated the first two items are the re- appropriations of the cash savings that has been set aside for the Smith Valley Road Project. Last year, it was recommended to do this method of re-appropriation, instead of encumbering, so that it doesn't show twice in the County's Fiscal Plan that their financial advisor Mike Reuter prepares each year. Mr. Bates asked when this comes to fruition, does the State kick in any money. Mr. Mastin replied there is no State money for this project. He explained the bulk of the expense will come from the bond; once the bond is complete, expenses will be paid from these two line items. Mr. Mallers inquired if the bond issuance has occurred yet. Mr. Mastin replied yes; it happened in October 2025. Mr. Mallers then asked what the general timeline looks like for this project. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 3 of 12 Mr. Mastin explained they are neck deep in development; they are in the right-of-way acquisition process right now, which will be a long process. They have started seeing some of the appraisals come through and they are moving forward. Mr. Bates asked if this was from St Rd 135 to the interstate. Mr. Mastin replied yes. More specifically, it is from the Mullinix Road round-about to Restin Road (the entrance to Carefree South). They are also coordinating with INDOT, who is designing an intersection improvement project at Smith Valley and St Rd 135, to make sure these two projects tie into together. Mr. Ditmars wanted to clarify that the use of the bond funds will be used first and then these two line items, noting these amounts most likely will carry over to 2027. Mr. Mastin concurred. Mrs. Burton made a motion to approve the two following requests as presented: (2a) AA: 1001.49152.00000.0201 Smith Valley Road (3a) AA: 1112.49152.00000.0201 Smith Valley Road Mr. Mailers seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. 4. Cumulative Bridge #1135) Highway Mr. Mastin was also present for these requests. Mrs. Graves asked to take items 4a & 4b separately. $12,000,000.00 $15,000,000.00 Mr. Mastin stated the request is for a part time engineer that was discussed toward the end of last year. He does have a part time engineer job description (was in February council packet). He stated they hired a part time engineer last year and it is working out great. He noted the bulk of the work they are doing is bridge and culvert related; therefore, they should be paid from this fund. Mrs. Graves stated since this fund is new again for 2026, there was really no Part Time line item to work with. She then inquired how he came up with the amount of $65,000 for this position. Mr. Mastin answered $65,000 was just a rough estimate for work done on an annual part time basis. In reality, he feels like it will be less than that. He also stated during a recent conversation with Mrs. Graves, that when this matter was discussed last year, he had stated about $40,000 a year would be needed and he was fine with lowering his request to the $40,000. He added at budget time he would re-evaluate how much actually should be budgeted for next year. Mr. Ditmars asked what the status was regarding hiring someone for this position. Mr. Mastin replied he hired someone and they started working in December. This person has brought a lot of knowledge, especially on the drainage side and the bridge and culvert side, which has been a significant help to them. Mr. Ditmars then asked what the number should be; an amount should be known since the person has been working since December. Mr. Mastin explained he has paying this position from the MVH Fund, but is requesting it be paid from the Cumulative Bridge Fund. The amount would be the maximum of that $40,000 for the remainder of the year. He will monitor the hours of this employee, who is semi-retired and only working part time. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 4 of 12 Mrs. Graves asked if the part time job description has been given to legal. Mr. Mastin replied yes. Mr. Ditmars made a motion to approve the request as revised. Mr. Bates seconded the motion, which carried unanimously. (4a) AA: 1135.11400.00000.0206 Part Time $ 65,000.00 40,000.00 (4b) 1135.11400.00000.0206 — Part Time - approval of $65.00/hr for a part time Engineer Mr. Myers inquired about cash flow since there are so many ongoing projects and asked when they would be completed. Mr. Mastin stated there was a resolution done at the beginning of the year to do a temporary loan from the Rainy Day Fund to the Cumulative Bridge Fund to help with cash flow. Approval of Resolution 2026-03: A Resolution of the Johnson County Council Approving the Execution of a Lease By and Between the Nineveh Fire Protection District, Johnson County, Indiana, and the Nineveh Fire Protection District Building Corporation for the Purpose of Funding the Construction of a New Fire Station Facility for the Nineveh Fire Protection District, Johnson County, Indiana Jeff Peters, from Peters Franklin and serving as the Municipal Advisor on the bonds for the Nineveh Fire Protection District (Nineveh FPD), was present for this request. He stated that the bond counsel and a member of the Nineveh FPD Board were also present. Mr. Peters stated this was first brought to the Council's attention last August. He explained this project started back in 2020; the fire district wants to replace its fire house, which was built in 1965 and won't house a modern fire truck. He stated it is well beyond its useful life and they are working on getting it replaced. There has been a lot of debate and input from taxpayers. The total project cost is now down to $4,070,000; the financing for this will be 20 years. The property tax repayments will begin in pay 2028, with the last payment to be made in January 2048. He explained the reason for the delay is because the amount of these bonds verses the current tax base in this area requires it to be set up as a lease rental with a building corporation. This is similar to what schools must do and what the County did last year with their Redevelopment Authority bonds (the Redevelopment Authority is basically the building corporation for the Redevelopment Commission). Mr. Peters stated when this is put on the tax rolls, it is estimated to be about 9.2 cents. He then gave the example: a homestead property assessed at $250,000, this would cost them about $116.00 a year. Mrs. Graves asked if this is the project that started with a $12 million+ number. Mr. Peters replied yes; however, that number was based on what they thought should be built to face current and future needs. It also included the cost of a new fire truck. He stated the fire truck has been removed from the current project cost and the project has been scaled back to what the fire district and taxpayers think will serve their needs. Brief discussion was held regarding the area where the station is located and the assessed values associated with it; more specifically how it affects the property taxes. Mr. Myers stated he would like to hear from the fire department on what this is going to do for them. Kevin Hendrickson, President of the Nineveh FPD, was present and stated he couldn't speak for the fire department, but from his perspective as a retired firefighter, this will improve a lot of things. First, just the building itself - when they look to buy equipment, they have to spec it because it just won't house what is out there and available today. Second, when it freezes outside, their building freezes and the toilets freeze. There is water in the bay; there is mold and just a ton of issues with the building itself. He then stated with the evacuation systems that are out there today to keep Council Regular Meeting Minutes — March 9, 2026 Page 8 of 12 the carcinogens off the fire fighters, this new facility will house that and improve their health. As far as their equipment goes, that is another hurdle they will need to jump through, being diligent with that funding when buying a new fire truck. Mrs. Burton commented she and a few other council members spent an afternoon at the current fire station in Nineveh, and in her opinion, it is as bad as it can get and doesn't know how it hasn't been condemned yet. She commends the firefighters for making it work. Mr. Ditmars agreed something needs to be done, but there is nothing they can do regarding the democratic process in that geographical area. It is at a point now where both the taxpayers and the district are in agreement on an amount. He doesn't feel like the people are happy with the tax increase, but understand the need for the service it provides. Mrs. Burton expressed the County Council is just the governing body for this; they have no input on what happens - is that correct? Max Adams, from Barnes & Thornburgh and serving as the bond counsel for the Nineveh FPD, was present to explain that the County Council's role outside of the annual appropriations and budgeting is to approve the lease/bond issuance. Mrs. Graves inquired about requests for the $13,750 for Food and the $8,000 for Travel & Training. Ms. Bruther explained that one of the components of the Trust Based Relation Intervention (TBRI) is cultural; it is a paradigm they have implemented across all of the juvenile justice and adult juvenile justice systems on how the staff interacts with the juveniles. This grant allows for snacks and water to both staff and participants as part of the wellness (nutrition/hydration) during the programs and office visits. She noted they also have a Blessing Box outside of their building they stock for the community. She added a small portion of these funds are used for when they have collaborative meetings. Ms. Bruther then stated the funds for Travel & Training will be used for a conference in October where seven Juvenile staff members will attend (in Plainfield), which is a requirement of being part of JDAI. She noted they received another grant from the State of Indiana to attend a conference (located somewhere around the Plainfield area) in February to implement TBRI Practitioner Training in the state of Indiana. This other grant will allow for 100 practitioners to be trained at this conference; Johnson County will be allowed 10 of those 100 spots. The 10 participants will have additional travel and lodging expenses, which will be paid from this grant (the other grant is paying for the actual training/conference). Mrs. Graves asked if this grant could offset any expenses that are currently budgeted in the General Fund. Brief discussion was held regarding using grant funds to help reduce expenses in the General Fund. Ms. Bruther replied this grant is specific in its use for JDAI purposes. Mrs. Burton made a motion to approve the requests as presented. Mr. Bates seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. items.title: September 14, 2026 Council Minutes
items.text: COUNTY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING -SEPTEMBER 14, 2026 The meeting was called to order by Council President, Michele Ann Graves. A. Call the Meeting to Order 1. Roll Call The following members were present: Jonathan Myers, Melinda Griesemer, John Mailers, Pamela Burton, John Ditmars, and Ron Bates. 2. Invocation Mrs. Burton gave the invocation. 3. Pledge of Allegiance Mrs. Graves led the Pledge of Allegiance. 4. Approval of 9/14/26 Agenda Mrs. Graves stated the following amendments to the agenda: 1. Remove item El — Clerk's request to increase hourly rate of Absentee Voter Board 2. Move up Item F, Other Business — Approval of Ordinance 2026-10, to be heard after item D - Routine Matters due to scheduling issue Mr. Bates made a motion to approve the agenda as amended. Mr. Myers seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. 5. Public Comments (agenda items only, limited to 5 minutes per person) There were no public comments. B. First Preliminary Determination Public Hearing on the General Obligation Bonds, Series 2026 Mrs. Graves opened the public hearing at 6:00pm to receive comment on County Council Ordinance 2026-09, an Ordinance of the Johnson County Council authorizing the issuance of General Obligation Bonds for the purpose of providing funds to acquire vehicles, acquire and install certain equipment, complete certain projects, and make certain improvements and renovations and to pay the costs of issuance of the bonds. She then invited Jeff Peters, Municipal Advisor, to discuss some required disclosures. Mr. Peters was present and stated that since this is a controlled project the following disclosures are required: 1. The percent of the County's current and projected annual debt service payments divided by the net assessed value of the taxable property within the County (the "Net Assessed Value") is approximately 0.0713%. 2. The percent of the County's outstanding long-term debt coupled with the outstanding long-term debt of other taxing units located within the County divided by the Net Assessed Value is approximately 6.0888%. 3. The maximum term of the bonds is 8 years. 4. The maximum principal amount of bonds is $7,835,000. 5. The estimated interest rate on the bonds is 5.00%. 6. The estimated total interest cost for the bonds is $385,688. 7. The description of the projects to be financed with bond proceeds include: vehicles, county park, county fairground, highway equipment, north annex, and various other projects and equipment. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — September 14, 2026 Page 1 of .5 8. The following statement must be provided: If the County Council adopts a resolution making a preliminary determination following the second public hearing on October 12th, a notice of that determination would be published and property owners or registered voters would have 30 days following the publication to file a petition requesting the application of the petition remonstrance process for the proposed bonds. 9. The County's current debt service levy is $7,030,377 and the current debt service rate is $0. 0530 cents per $100 of assessed valuation. 10. If the bonds are issued, the estimated increase to the debt service levy is $24,811 and the tax rate is $0.0183 cents per $100 of assessed valuation. 11. The estimated increase to the County's debt service levy and rate that will result during the following ten (10) years if the County issues the bonds, after also considering any changes that will occur to the debt service levy and rate during that period on account of any outstanding bonds or lease obligations that will mature or terminate during that period. a. Based on currently outstanding debt: in 2027, an estimated levy is approximately $7,055,188 and a rate of $.0549, and for 2028, an estimated levy of $1,738,000 and a rate of $0.0135. Mr. Peters then stated he would be happy to answer any questions they may have. Mrs. Graves thanked Mr. Peters. She then stated members of the public appearing at the meeting either in person or via zoom have the right to be heard and opened the floor for any public comments. Hearing none, she closed the public comment portion of the hearing. C. Approval of Ordinance 2026-09 (First Reading): An Ordinance of the Johnson County Council Authorizing the Issuance of General Obligation Bonds for the Puipose of Providing Funds to Acquire Vehicles, Acquire and Install Certain Equipment, Complete Certain Projects and Make Certain Improvements and Renovations and to Pay the Costs of Issuance of the Bonds Mr. Ditmars made a motion to approve Ordinance 2026-09 as presented on first reading. Mr. Mallers seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. D. Any items listed on the consent agenda may be removed by a Council member and moved to the regular agenda. Mr. Myers made a motion to approve the consent agenda as presented. Mrs. Burton made a motion to approve the above requests as presented. Mr. Ditmars seconded the motion, which carried unanimously. F. Other Business 1. Approval of Ordinance 2026-10: An Ordinance of the Johnson County Council Approving an Additional Appropriation of Certain Proceeds from the Issuance of General Obligation Bonds of the Nineveh Fire Protection District, Johnson County, Indiana (Series 2026A Bonds — Fire Station Project; $1,120,000) - Second Reading Mr. Myers made a motion to approve Ordinance 2026-10 as presented. Mr. Bates seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. Council Regular Meeting Minutes — September 14, 2026 Page 3 of5 Mr. Myers asked if there were scheduled dates for the start/finish of these two projects. G. Old & New Business 1. Sheriff— Reclassification of Position - acct#13200 Crime Technician Chief Deputy Sheriff, Andy Barnhart, was present to request a reclassification of a position due to a long-time employee who is retiring in December and will be replaced with an existing employee. This is something that was brought up a few years ago but hasn't been discussed again since then because no employees' salary was being affected — until now. This transition for the existing employee should have been more of a lateral move; however, due to the classification, the retired Crime Technician employee was making more than the WIS study. He knows job classification reviews are to be done in November but is asking for this to be sent earlier to WIS in time for the upcoming budget and before it would affect the existing employee's salary who will be moving into the Crime Technician position. Mr. Barnhart stated the position of Crime Technician was classified as a CIV POLE 1 solely due to an inaccurate and outdated job description. They are asking for the job to be reclassified as a CIV POLE 5. Mrs. Graves stated the reason they can allow this request outside of their normal process is because it is in compliance with the Council's reclassification ordinance in reviewing a position when it becomes vacant due to a separating employee. In this case, the position is held by a longtime employee who is retiring December 18'1'. The reclassification request is to reflect the actual requirements of the position in its current usage. So, the position has been doing the work, even though the work is not in the job description. And, because it is a restructuring, that is why the Council can conform to their process and send this to WIS now for review She also said, for the record, all communication with WIS needs to go through County Legal, per the Council's contract. Mr. Ditmars made a motion to approve the request as presented. Mr. Bates seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. 2. Discussion of New Hires — Employee Salaries (from Auzust Meeting) Mrs. Graves stated this was discussed at last month's meeting; however, a final vote was not taken. The discussion was for clarity regarding the Council's position with new hires' conforming to the W1S salary guidelines and salary ranges. This topic was addressed last year at budget time: however, the Auditor's Office has reported that not everyone understood the instruction and there was need for clarity. Mrs. Graves then stated the motion would be: effective immediately, all new employees and current employees transferring into a new position will be compensated according to the appropriate WIS job classification within the approved salary range for that classification and not automatically paid the previous incumbent's salary if that salary exceeds the WIS guidelines. New Probation Officers will be compensated according to the 2026 minimum salary schedule for Probation Officers by the Judicial Conference of Indiana. She then asked for a motion. Mr. Bates made a motion to approve the language as read by Mrs. Graves. Mrs. Burton seconded the motion, which carried unanimously. H. Adjournment — Next regular meeting October 12, 2026 There being no further business, Mr. Myers made a motion to adjourn. Mr. Mailers seconded the motion, which unanimously carried. items.title: Ordinance 2026-O-7: An Ordinance Amending Title 25 of the Johnson County Code of Ordinances
items.text: ORDINANCE NO. 2026-O-7 AN ORDINANCE AMENDING TITLE 25 OF THE JOHNSON COUNTY CODE OF ORDINANCES WHEREAS, Indiana Code§ 36-1-3 et. seq. permits any unit in the State of Indiana to exercise any power or to perform any function necessary to the public interest in the context of its governmental or internal affairs, which is not prohibited by the Constitution of the United States or of the State of Indiana, or denied or pre-empted by any other law, or is not expressly granted by any other law to another governmental entity; and WHEREAS, the Board of Commissioners of Johnson County, Indiana is the executive body under Ind. Code § 36-2-2-2 and is by law authorized to adopt ordinances for the protection of the public health, safety, and general welfare of its residents; and WHEREAS, the purpose of this Ordinance is to regulate peddling in Johnson County and clarify the penalties for violations of this Chapter BE IT THEREFORE ORDAINED BY THE BOARD THAT: Johnson County Code § 25-2-1-4 be amended as follows: § 25-2-1-4 GENERAL PROHIBITIONS; PENALTIES. (A) No person shall: 1. With or without a license, enter upon private property where any form of sticker or sign is clearly displayed advising that the occupant does not wish to be called upon by peddlers, canvassers, and/or solicitors, such as a “No Soliciting” sign; 2. With or without a license, remove any sign or sticker that gives notice that the occupant does not wish to be called upon by peddlers, canvassers, and/or solicitors; 3. With or without a license, distribute any commercial or non-commercial literature at any private property in a manner that causes permanent damage to such property; or 4. With or without a license, remain on private property after being asked by the occupant to leave. COMMISSIONERS Brian P. Baird, Chairman, 2025-2028 Kevin M. Walls, Member, 2023-2026 Ronald H. West, Member, 2025-2028 County Attorney Tiffany M. Costley Assistant County Attorney Taylor E. Webster ADDRESS 86 West Court Street Franklin, Indiana 46131 Phone (317) 346-4300 Fax (317) 736-8066 Website: www.johnsoncounty.in.gov BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS JOHNSON COUNTY ORDINANCE NO. 2026-O-7 AN ORDINANCE AMENDING TITLE 25 OF THE JOHNSON COUNTY CODE OF ORDINANCES Any person violating the provisions of this Subsection (A) may be subject to criminal penalties under Indiana Code. (B) No person shall: 1. With or without a license, use, or attempt to use, any entrance other than the front or main entrance to the dwelling except by express invitation of the occupant of the property; or 2. Engage in peddling activities as defined above without first obtaining a license from the Johnson County Sheriff’s Office. Any person violating the provisions of this Subsection (B) shall be subject to the following fines (escalation on a calendar year basis): First Offense: $50.00 Second Offense: $150.00 Third Offense: $300.00 Subsequent Offenses: $1,000.00 Multiple citations may be issued on the same day, if more than one offense occurs. Repeat

items.title: Notice of Availability of ADA Self-Evaluation and Transition Plan 8/31/26 thru 9/15/26 and Public Meeting on 9/14/26
items.text: NOTICE OF AVAILABILITY OF ADA SELF-EVALUATION AND TRANSITION PLAN & PUBLIC MEETING Johnson County has conducted a Self-Evaluation of all County-owned facilities and all County programs for compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and prepared a draft Transition Plan describing the results of the self-evaluation. Title II of the ADA requires that each of the County’s services, programs, and activities be readily accessible and usable by individuals with disabilities. Copies of the draft Self-Evaluation and Transition Plan will be available for public review at the following locations in Franklin between August 31st, 2026, and September 15th, 2026.  County Annex (Commissioners/ADA Coordinator’s Office) -86 W. Court St, Franklin, IN 46131  Public Library (Circulation Desk, Franklin, Branch) – 401 State St, Franklin, IN 46131 Comments can be provided, in writing, by the deadline of September 15th, 2026, at 5 p.m. to Barbara Davis, ADA Coordinator, in person, via email to bdavis@JohnsonCounty.in.gov , or via US Mail. In addition, the County has scheduled a meeting to solicit public input and comment on the Transition Plan, and will consist of a short presentation at the beginning of the meeting to provide information on the Transition Plan, followed by open discussion and interaction with attendees. This will be an opportunity for the community to ask questions as well as provide suggestions and comments on the draft Self-Evaluation and Transition Plan. All comments will be reviewed, considered and included in the appendix of the document. The meeting will be held in the auditorium at the County Annex building, 86 W. Court St., on September 14th, 2026, at 5:00pm. Johnson County complies with the ADA. Upon request, the County will provide written materials in appropriate alternative formats, or disability-related modification or accommodation, including auxiliary aids or services, to enable individuals with disabilities to participate in public input. Please send a written request, including your name, mailing address, phone number, and brief description of the requested accommodation at least three (3) business days prior to the close of the comment period to the ADA Coordinator in the Commissioner’s Office at the Courthouse Annex (86 W. Court St., Franklin, IN 46131).

items.title: Notice to Bidders – JC Park Banquet Hall – DUE 10/19/2026 by 10:00 a.m.
items.text: NOTICE TO BIDDERS Notice is hereby given that Johnson County, Indiana, acting by and through its Board of Commissioners, will receive sealed bids at the Office of the Auditor in Johnson County Courthouse West Annex, 86 West Court Street, Franklin, for the Johnson County Park Banquet Hall Project in Nineveh Indiana. Bids are due no later than 10:00 a.m. (local time) on Monday, October 19, 2026. Bids received after this time will be returned unopened. E- mailed or faxed bids will not be accepted. Drawings, Specifications, Instruction to Bidders, and Bid Forms will be ready September 28, 2026, and may be obtained by contacting Wes Harrison, County Project Manager, at wharrison@lhb-eng.com or (317) 431-3863. Bid security in the amount of 2% of the bid amount, including alternates, must accompany each bid in accordance with the Instruction to Bidders. Bid Security shall be in the form of a bid bond, cashier’s check, or certified check which shall be payable to the Board of Commissioners of Johnson County, Indiana. The successful bidder will be required to furnish performance and payment bonds for one hundred percent (100%) of the contract price prior to the execution of contracts. There will be a non-mandatory pre-bid meeting on October 6 at 11:00 pm at the Johnson County Park Office at 3060 East North Street, Nineveh, Indiana 46164. The Commissioners reserve the right to accept or reject and bid and to waive any irregularities in bidding. All bids may be held for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days before awarding contracts.

items.title: Board of Zoning Appeals | Town of Prince’s Lakes
items.text:
Board of Zoning Appeals
The Board of Zoning Appeals meets to approve or deny variances from the development standards (such as height, bulk or area) of the zoning ordinance. They approve or deny all special exceptions, special uses, contingent uses and conditional uses pertaining to cases or the particular situations specified in the zoning ordinance.
The Board of Zoning Appeals shall hear and determine appeals from and review:
(1) any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by an administrative official, hearing officer, or staff member under the zoning ordinance;
(2) any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by an administrative board or other body except a plan commission in relation to the enforcement of the zoning ordinance; or

The Prince's Lakes Park Board was initiated in November 2023 by our Town Council to create a master plan for our parks. CATALYTIC CONVERTER PACKET
CATALYTIC CONVERTER SALE REQUIREMENTS
The sale of a converter without a dealer license requires the police to inspect the converter and the vehicle it came off. This is done by cutting the converter off in the presence of law enforcement or having a law enforcement officer view the vehicle that the converter was cut off of to match the converter being sold. The law enforcement officer can complete a reporting showing that the converter has been verified as not stolen and able to be sold with the Make Model and VIN the converter was removed from. This report shall be taken to a Core Buyer of their choice and then sold.
Any law enforcement agency can inspect the vehicle and converter and complete the report. If the vehicle and converter are not present together then Edinburgh Police will not complete the report for sale.

PUBLIC NOTICE
The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (“ADA”)
In accordance with the requirements of Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (“ADA”), The Town of Edinburgh will not discriminate against qualified individuals with disabilities on the basis of disability in its services, programs, or activities.
Employment
The Town of Edinburgh Indiana does not discriminate on the basis of disability in its hiring or employment practices and complies with all federal and state law requirements.
Effective Communication
The Town of Edinburgh Indiana will generally, upon request, provide appropriate aids and services leading to effective communication for qualified persons with disabilities so they can participate equally in town programs, services, and activities.
Modifications to Policies and Procedures
The Town of Edinburgh Indiana will make all reasonable modifications to policies and programs to ensure that people with disabilities have an equal opportunity to enjoy all of its programs, services, and activities.
Anyone who requires an auxiliary aid or service for effective communication, or a modification of policies or procedures to participate in a program, service, or activity of the town, should contact the office of the program, service or activity coordinator as soon as possible but no later than 48 hours before the scheduled event.
The ADA does not require the town to take any action that would fundamentally alter the nature of its programs or services, or impose an undue financial or administrative burden.
Complaints that a program, service, or activity of the Town of Edinburgh Indiana is not accessible to persons with disabilities should be directed to:
ADA Coordinator: Mary Patterson
Address: 107 S. Holland St.
Edinburgh, IN 46124
E-Mail: mpatterson@edinburgh.in.us
Phone: (812) 526-3510 TTY: 711
The Town of Edinburgh is working diligently toward bringing the town facilities into compliance with the ADA requirements. If anyone has any areas within town they feel are not accessible or have been denied access to due to having a disability, please see our ADA Grievance Procedures below and the ADA Grievance Form which can be filled out and returned to the Edinburgh ADA Coordinator for processing.

Board Members
The Trafalgar Local Board of Finance is responsible for overseeing the financial management and investment practices of the Town of Trafalgar. The board ensures transparency, accountability, and compliance in all financial matters. Members are appointed by the Town Council and typically include current members of the council.
Our Responsibilities
Investment Oversight Reviews and approves the Town’s investment strategies and ensures public funds are managed responsibly.
Annual Reporting Receives and reviews financial reports prepared by the Clerk-Treasurer, including fund balances, interest earnings, and financial planning updates.
Policy Review & Compliance Ensures that financial practices align with state regulations, local ordinances, and industry best practices.
Fiscal Accountability Promotes transparency and long-term financial stability through responsible stewardship of public resources.

Trafalgar Park Board
Board Members
The Trafalgar Park Board is appointed by the Town Council and plays a vital role in shaping the community’s parks and recreational spaces. The Board consists of four members who must be residents of the Town and are selected based on their interest in and knowledge of parks and recreation. No more than two members may be affiliated with the same political party unless the Town Council grants a waiver, as allowed under IND. CODE § 36-10-3-4.1 . Initial Board members served staggered terms of one, two, three, and four years, after which all members are appointed to four-year terms, with terms expiring on the first Monday in January; members continue in office until their successors are appointed, in accordance with IND. The Trafalgar Redevelopment Commission (RDC) is dedicated to fostering economic development, revitalizing key areas, and strategically guiding long-term infrastructure improvements in the Town of Trafalgar. The RDC plays a vital role in managing Tax Increment Financing (TIF) districts and supporting projects that align with the town’s vision for responsible growth.
Responsibilities of the RDC
Promote commercial and industrial development
Oversee reinvestment of TIF funds
Evaluate and implement redevelopment plans
Support infrastructure enhancements within designated areas
Collaborate with stakeholders to attract business and support job creation

Planning Commission – Town of Trafalgar
The Town of Trafalgar Planning Commission guides the town’s physical growth and land use in alignment with its comprehensive plan. The Commission reviews subdivision plats, zoning changes, development plans, and other proposals to ensure that new development is orderly, sustainable, and serves the public interest.
Our Responsibilities
Review and approve subdivision and site development plans
Make recommendations to the Town Council on zoning ordinances and amendments
Evaluate land use proposals and development patterns
Ensure that growth aligns with the Town of Trafalgar’s long-term goals and comprehensive plan

items.title: Economic Development Commission Detailed Overview
items.text: Town of Whiteland Economic Development Commission (ORD 2003-07) Primary function of an economic development commission is to permit the use of conduit financing to enable private companies to borrow funds using the municipality’s name (usually to benefit from the municipality’s tax exempt status or the TIF generated by the private development) to finance economic development projects. Composition of Membership The members of the economic development commission shall be appointed by the town executive. One (1) of the members shall be selected by the town executive, one (1) shall be nominated by the fiscal body of the county in which the town is located, and one (1) shall be nominated by the town fiscal body. (I.C. 36-7-12-6) The economic development commissioners shall take office upon their appointment, and their terms run from February 1 after their original appointment, for a period of: (1) three (3) years, if selected by the town executive; (2) two (2) years, if nominated by the town fiscal body; and (3) one (1) year, if nominated by the county fiscal body. Responsibilities An economic development commission shall investigate, study, and survey the need for additional job opportunities, industrial diversification, water services, and pollution control facilities in the unit, and shall recommend action to improve or promote job opportunities, industrial diversification, water services, and availability of pollution control facilities in the unit. Specific Responsibilities for the Town of Whiteland EDC: • make direct loans to users or developers for the cost of acquisition, construction, or installation of economic development or pollution control facilities, including land, machinery, or equipment, with the loans to be secured by the pledge of one (1) or more taxable or tax-exempt bonds or other secured or unsecured debt obligations of the users or developers; • enter into agreements with users or developers to allow the users or developers to wholly or partially construct economic development or pollution control facilities to be acquired by the unit; • issue taxable or tax -exempt bonds under this chapter for single or multiple, identified or unidentified, economic development or pollution control facilities to accomplish the purposes of this chapter, and secure their payment as provided in this chapter; • establish reserves from the proceeds of the sale of taxable or tax -exempt bonds, other funds, or both, to secure the payment of the principal and interest on the bonds; • lend or deposit the proceeds of bonds to or with a lender for the purpose of furnishing funds to the lender for the purpose of making a loan to a specifically identified developer or user for the financing of specifically identified economic development or pollution control facilities under this chapter; and • reimburse from bond proceeds expe nditures for pollution control facilities or economic development facilities. items.title: Town of Whiteland: Redevelopment Commission
items.text:
The Redevelopment Commission (RDC) is charged with encouraging economic development opportunities in Whiteland by aiding new development and the redevelopment of underutilized sites. The Commission’s primary tool is the Tax Increment Financing (TIF) district, which they oversee in conjunction with the Town Council.
Members
RDC members are appointed annually. Three are appointed by the Town Council President, and two are appointed by the Town Council. A non-voting representative of the school board also participates in Commission business.
David Hawkins – President

Term 6/30/2025 – 6/30/2027 – Appointed by Clark-Pleasant Community School Corporation School Board
Meetings
Redevelopment Commission meetings are regularly scheduled on the second Thursday of each month at 6pm.
Reports
By state statute, there are two annual reports required to be prepared by every redevelopment commission. The first is required to be filed with the Town Council President by March 15 and largely describes the operations of the Commission in the previous year. The other must be filed with the Town Council by August 1 and presents the financial status of each TIF district in the town (currently, there is only one). A third report, from the Council to the Department of Local Government Finance, is due by October 1 and is a compilation of the August 1 report(s) in the state’s prescribed format.

items.title: Town of Whiteland: Board of Zoning Appeals
items.text:
The Whiteland Advisory Board of Zoning Appeals (“BZA”) works to ensure that zoning regulations are fairly applied across varying properties in town. Essentially, the BZA serves as a board to hear appeals that specific zoning regulations should be applied differently to a particular property due to certain conditions of the site or the proposed use. The administrative appeal is an appeal of a decision made by town staff regarding the zoning code. The BZA does not enforce the zoning code, but they can adjust the regulations for a property to suit its specific site conditions that would otherwise be in violation of the zoning code. The responsibilities of the BZA is as follows:
Indiana Code provides that the BZA has the following specific authorities:
Granting of variances Developmental standards variances Variances of use
Developmental standards variances
Variances of use
Granting of special exceptions (also known as conditional uses)
Appeals from administrative decisions
Members
Two members of the BZA are selected from the Plan Commission, two are appointed by the Town Council President, and one is appointed by the Town Council. By state code, members cannot hold any other elected or appointed position (except the two Plan Commission members).

Welcome to Whiteland
2025 Year in Review
The Town’s free residential brush and limb service will be adjusted to a monthly schedule beginning in December 2026 . To ease into the adjusted pickup schedule, in October & November, pick up will move to twice a month, occurring on the 2 nd and 4 th week of the month. Monthly pickups will begin in December, occurring on the 2 nd week of each month. We ask that you place your brush at the curb by Monday morning of the scheduled pickup week.
As a reminder we will only pick up brush or limbs that are 8” in diameter or smaller. No ornamental grasses, limbs larger than 8” in diameter, or tree trunks will be picked up .
Please note – if there are any extreme wind or weather conditions that require additional brush and limb pick up, the Town of Whiteland will provide additional pickup services.

items.title: IHSAA Physical Form
items.text: 1. The most current version of the IHSAA PPE Form must be used and may not be altered or modified in any manner. 2. The PPE Form must be signed by a physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner or physician assistant only after the medical history is reviewed, the examination performed, and the PPE Form completed in its entirety. No pre-signed or pre-stamped forms will be accepted. 3. SIGNATURES  The signature must be hand-written. No signature stamps will be accepted.  The signature and license number must be affixed on page three (3).  The parent signatures must be affixed to the form on pages two (2) and five (5).  The student-athlete signature must be affixed to pages two (2) and five (5). 4. Distribution  History Form retained by Physician/Healthcare Provider  Examination Form and Consent and Release Form signed and returned to member school. Your cooperation will help ensure the best medical screening for Indiana’s high school athletes. PRE-PARTICIPATION PHYSICAL EVALUATION FORM (PPE) The IHSAA Pre-participation Physical Evaluation (PPE) is the ﬁ rst and most important step in providing for the well-being of Indiana’s high school athletes. The form is designed to identify risk factors prior to athletic participation by way of a thorough medical history and physical ex- amination. The IHSAA, under the guidance of the Indiana State Medical Association’s Commit- tee on Sports Medicine, requires that the PPE Form be signed by a physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner or physician a ssistant holding a license to practice in the State of Indiana. In order to assure that these rigorous standards are met, both organizations endorse the following require-ments for completion of the PPE Form: Cover PREPARTICIPATION PHYSICAL HISTORY FORM Note: Complete and sign this form (with your parents if younger than 18) before your appointment. History Form is retained by physician/healthcare provider. Name: Date of birth: Date of examination: Sex assigned at birth (F , M, or intersex): Grade: How do you identify your gender? (F , M, or other): List past and current medical conditions. Have you ever had surgery? It yes, list all past surgical procedures. Medicines and supplements: List all current prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, and supplements (herbal and nutritional). Do you have any allergies? If yes, please list all your allergies (ie. Medicines, pollens, food, stinging insects). Are your required vaccinations current? Patient Health Questionnaire Version 4 (PHQ-4) Overall, during the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems? (Circle Response.) 🧡💙 In Case You Missed It: What a Week to Be a Warrior! A county championship 34 years in the making, an incredible conference winning streak, and talented young musicians taking the stage alongside community performers! It's been an exciting few days across Clark-Pleasant, and we have some amazing student accomplishments to celebrate! 🏆 WCHS CROSS COUNTRY MAKES HISTORY! For the first time since 1992, the Whiteland Community High School girls cross country team is bringing home the Johnson County Championship! The Lady Warriors delivered an outstanding performance at Saturday's Johnson County Championships, with five runners finishing in the top 10! 🥈 Lena Shipp – 2nd Place 🥉 Gabi Goedeker – 3rd Place 🏅 Abby Boner – 4th Place 🏅 Eden Muhlhauser – 9th Place 🏅 Claire Proctor – 10th Place And the excitement didn't stop there! 🥇 Colton Watson claimed the Johnson County Individual Championship with a time of 15:52, continuing his undefeated season! The WCHS boys team also earned a third-place finish. Congratulations to our Warrior runners and coaches on an incredible weekend! 🎾 WCHS TENNIS CONTINUES ITS WINNING TRADITION! The Whiteland Community High School boys tennis team has plenty to celebrate after defeating Perry Meridian 5-0 on Thursday! With that victory, the Warriors completed their FOURTH consecutive undefeated conference season! The varsity team has now won 62 of its last 63 conference matches and has captured the conference championship in six of the last seven seasons! And the JV team? They're making history of their own! After a 7-2 victory over Perry Meridian, the JV Warriors have now won an incredible 76 consecutive conference matches! Their last conference loss was in 2016! Congratulations to Coach Mike Gillespie and our Warrior tennis players on these remarkable accomplishments! 🎶 CPMS MUSICIANS TAKE THE STAGE! On Sunday, six talented Clark-Pleasant Middle School band students were selected to perform alongside the Greater Greenwood Community Band during its Side-by-Side Concert at the Surina Park Amphitheater! Congratulations to our CPMS musicians: 🎵 Zayn Cannoot 🎵 Brayden Roy 🎵 Nathan Vierling 🎵 Everett Wyant 🎵 Corbin Sefton 🎵 David Canizares What a wonderful opportunity for these young musicians to share their talents with our community and perform alongside experienced musicians! 🧡💙 From historic championships and incredible winning streaks to outstanding musical performances, our Warriors continue to give us so much to celebrate! 📣 Want to keep up with Warrior Athletics? Be sure to follow the Whiteland Beat Sports Network for the latest high school athletic news, scores, highlights, and student-athlete accomplishments! A special thank you to the Whiteland Beat Sports Network for creating the graphics celebrating our historic weekend! #WarriorPride #ClarkPleasant #WhitelandWarriors

💙🧡 MEET OUR AMBASSADORS: HEATHER HOFMANN We're continuing to introduce you to the members of our 2026–27 Clark-Pleasant Ambassador Academy, and today we'd like you to meet Heather Hofmann! Heather is a mom of two young children, Hendrix and Lyn, and says her family is a huge part of who she is. She is a Certified Medical Assistant with a background in healthcare and a love for helping and connecting with people. Heather's connection to Clark-Pleasant began through her children, but she knew she wanted that connection to become something more. “As a parent, I want to be involved and do more than just drop my kids off and pick them up.” So, why Ambassador Academy? Heather wants to better understand the people, programs and opportunities that make Clark-Pleasant work—and find ways she can become more involved herself. For her, being part of a community means more than simply living in it. It means getting to know the people around you, understanding what's happening behind the scenes and being willing to find your own way to contribute. One thing Heather already appreciates is the sense of community she has experienced here. “As a parent, it means a lot to know that my children are growing up in an area where education, relationships, and supporting one another are valued.” Through Ambassador Academy, Heather hopes to learn more about the people, programs and partnerships supporting Clark-Pleasant students and families. Most importantly, she wants to become a better advocate for her own children and other families while discovering meaningful ways she can give back. And when Heather isn't working, learning or keeping up with two young kids, you'll probably find her outside! 🥾🌳 Heather loves hiking and exploring new places with her family. For her, getting outdoors is a chance to unplug, enjoy nature and make memories with Hendrix and Lyn—and she's always looking for their next adventure. We love that Heather isn't content to simply have her family be part of Clark-Pleasant. She wants to understand it, connect with it and find her own way to contribute to it. We're excited to have her learning alongside us this year! 👋 Welcome to Ambassador Academy, Heather! #ClarkPleasant #WarriorNation #AmbassadorAcademy #MeetOurAmbassadors

ABOUT CLARK-PLEASANT SCHOOLS
Located south of Indianapolis, our schools offer innovative academics, caring teachers and state-of-the-art facilities. While we are one of Indiana's fastest-growing school districts, we value our legacy rooted in our small rural beginnings of individualized attention and focus on each student.
From STEM to college-credit courses and career pathways, we open doors to every dream. A wide array of student clubs, athletics and school organizations (more than 135) help each child find their passion. Our athletic teams are among the most competitive in Indiana. Our district has been recognized as one of Indiana’s Best Communities for Music Education and has many students earning state music awards.
Our schools are safe and welcoming, offering strong support systems that nurture confidence and success in and out of the classroom.

items.text:
Directions/Parking/Drop-Off/Pick-Up
CGHS Pick-Up/Drop Off
Directions to CGHS
CGHS Daily/Event Parking
Traffic routes around the Center Grove High School have been updated for the 2025-26 school year. These changes are designed to improve safety, reduce traffic back-up on Morgantown Road, and improve traffic flow - based on feedback we received last year.
STUDENT DROP-OFF AND PICK-UP Parents dropping off and picking up students from Center Grove High School should enter the high school campus by turning off of Morgantown Road onto Pennington Drive. Traffic on Pennington will continue through the peanut-shaped roundabout to east of the Tennis Complex and into the lot between the Innovation Center and Baseball Field. (See map below.) Parents will then continue north through the lot to the exit and turn left (south) back onto Trojan Lane. They will travel west, past the Tennis Complex, and turn right (north) onto Victory Lane to enter the drop-off/pick-up line. Drop-off is at Door #9, the same as prior years. This is the only location where students should be dropped off at school. Parents will then exit the campus by following Victory Lane to the roundabout at the intersection with Trojan Lane and continue north to Stones Crossing Road.
STUDENT PARKING FOOTBALL STUDENT LOT: Students may enter the parking lot east of the football stadium from Morgantown Road. They should take Pennington Road straight through the peanut-shaped roundabout, and curve around to Trojan Lane. There is no access from the north on Trojan Lane before school to this lot. This is not a change from prior years, however, students will be permitted to exit via Morgantown or Stones Crossing after school this year. Please note that this traffic will merge at the roundabout with parent pick-up traffic and students exiting the north lots.
NORTH STUDENT LOTS: Students may enter the north student lots from Stones Crossing Road. They should turn onto Trojan Lane and turn right into the student lot. (This is not a change from prior years.) GATE RESTRICTIONS Gates will be down on Pennington Road at the peanut to restrict traffic from turning left onto Victory Lane and on Trojan Lane just south of the roundabout from 7:30-8:05 AM when school is in session. The Pennington Road gate will also be down from 2:15-3:15 PM.
DURING SCHOOL PICK-UP AND DROP-OFF During the school day, students who are dropped off and picked up for appointments or late arrivals should use Door #9 (Hall of Excellence), where they will check in with staff at the security vestibule. After 1:30 PM, students may be picked up for appointments from Door #1should use the front administrative entrance (Door #1) at the flagpole/electronic sign off of Morgantown Road. Parents who need to come into the building should also use Door #1.
AFTER SCHOOL ACTIVITY DROP-OFF AND PICK-UP Parents dropping off and picking up students of any age for activities at Center Grove High School must follow the traffic markings around the high school.

JACK RUSSELL President, CGCSC Board of School Trustees
Jack Russell is a long-time resident of the Center Grove community. He graduated from Center Grove High School in 1974. He is a graduate of Purdue University where he studied Elementary Education. After Purdue, Mr. Russell attended Butler University to study dance and acting.
Russell spent time traveling the country after graduation doing live shows at theme parks and dinner theaters. During that time, he would also substitute teach in the local school system. After a few years working as general manager in his family’s real estate and development business, Russell returned to the world of education to teach full-time. He also spent time substitute teaching while raising his son, Austin, whom he adopted from Paraguay. Austin is a 2013 Center Grove graduate.
Russell has been an active member of the Center Grove Education Foundation. He is also involved with the Center Grove Alumni and Friends group. Russell was elected to the Center Grove Board of School Trustees in 2010 and has served in various leadership positions, including as president in 2013.
SCOTT ALEXANDER Vice President, CGCSC Board of School Trustees
Scott Alexander is a 1991 graduate of Center Grove High School and a lifelong Center Grove resident. He received his bachelor’s degree from Purdue University in 1995. Mr. Alexander is the Vice President, of Sales and Strategic Partnerships for InTempo Software.
Alexander joined Center Grove’s Board of School Trustees in 2010. Prior to that he was a four-year member of the Center Grove Education Foundation.
Alexander's Information Technology background spans over the past 18 years with experience in various leadership roles. He has spent a large portion of his career in the pharmaceutical and healthcare industries with some experience in consulting as well. Alexander brings vast experience in leading teams and businesses of varying sizes through information technology, operations, and logistics.
Alexander and his wife, Dana, have two sons who are graduates of Center Grove High School. In his spare time, he enjoys playing golf.
JANE DUNIGAN-SMITH Secretary, CGCSC Board of School Trustees
Jane Dunigan-Smith has lived in the Center Grove community for more than 22 years. She is the Senior Vice President and Chief Strategy Officer at BioCrossroads. Dunigan-Smith has a master’s degree in business administration, marketing and strategy and a bachelor’s degree in accounting and finance from the Kelley School of Business at Indiana University, Bloomington.
Dunigan-Smith has served on the Board of the Center Grove Education Foundation and is a graduate of the Center Grove Ambassadors program. She and her husband, Rodney, have two sons, one graduate of Center Grove High School (CGHS) and a senior at CGHS.
